# Text to 3D
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/text-to-3d

# Text to 3D

Turn a written description into a 3D model when you have an idea but no reference image.

Text to 3D works well for exploring concepts, prototyping, and trying several design directions. If you have a reference image, [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) matches it more closely. To brainstorm in a chat before you generate, use [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent). Meshy makes models for art and games, not CAD-precision engineering parts.

---

## Generate a model from text
To generate a model from text, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Model**.

2. At the top of the panel, click the **Text to 3D** tab.

3. Select **High Detail** for a detailed mesh, or **Smart Topology** for fewer polygons and cleaner topology.

4. Choose the AI model or topology:

   - If you selected **High Detail**, in the model list, select **Meshy 6** or **Meshy 6 Lite**.

   - If you selected **Smart Topology**, which uses Meshy T1, under **Topology**, select **Quad** or **Triangle**.

5. In **Prompt**, describe the object in up to 800 characters. A detailed prompt names these parts:

   - The subject: "a medieval castle tower"

   - The material: "stone walls with moss"

   - The art style: "low-poly game art style"

   - The scale: "roughly 3 meters tall"

6. Optional: Set **Pose** to **A-Pose** or **T-Pose** for a character you plan to rig. Pose needs a paid plan, and free accounts get a limited number of free tries. With Meshy 6, you can also turn on **Split** to split the model into parts, or set **Number of Generations** to get up to 10 models from one prompt. More than one generation needs a paid plan.

7. Click **Generate**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you generate. A Meshy 6 model takes about a minute, and a Smart Topology model about 3 minutes.

8. In the viewer, rotate and zoom to check the model.

The result is a mesh without textures. From the toolbar, you can texture, remesh, or download it.

![Meshy Text to 3D workspace: a text prompt for a medieval castle tower generates a low-poly 3D model, shown with topology stats and printability check](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/text-to-3d-p0-1.webp)

---

## Settings and tradeoffs
The following table shows what each choice trades off.

| Setting | Options | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model type | High Detail or Smart Topology | High Detail gives more detail and more faces. Smart Topology gives fewer faces and cleaner topology, which suits games. |
| AI model | Meshy 6 or Meshy 6 Lite | Meshy 6 gives higher quality and a stable structure for 20 credits. Meshy 6 Lite is faster and costs 10 credits. |
| Art style | Set in the prompt | "Realistic" produces high detail. "Stylized" or "cartoon" yields cleaner topology. |

---

## Examples
A specific prompt gives the AI enough to work with:

- Prompt: "a detailed steampunk pocket watch with gears visible through glass, brass and copper materials, realistic style"

- Result: a clean mesh with accurate gear details and about 25,000 faces.

A one-word prompt leaves the AI to guess:

- Prompt: "watch"

- Result: a wristwatch with little detail.

- Fix: name the type of watch, its materials, its style, and the features you want to see.

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The model doesn't match the description | The prompt is too vague | Add details: materials, style, viewpoint, and colors. |
| The model has floating fragments | The prompt describes several separate objects | Describe one subject per prompt. |
| The mesh has too many triangles | AI-generated meshes are dense | Use [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) to rebuild the topology. |
| Texture seams are visible | The UV layout has issues | Use [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing) to regenerate the textures. |

---

## FAQ
### How does Text to 3D work in Meshy?

Describe an object in words, and Meshy generates a 3D model from the description. You don't need a reference image.

### How do I write a good text-to-3D prompt?

Combine the subject, its material, the art style, and technical details, for example "a medieval castle tower, stone walls with moss, low-poly game art."

### How many credits does Text to 3D cost?

A Meshy 6 generation costs 20 credits, Meshy 6 Lite costs 10, and a Smart Topology generation with Meshy T1 costs 20. The panel shows the cost before you generate.

### Can I use Meshy 7.1 for Text to 3D?

No. Meshy 7.1 generates from images, so it's available in Image to 3D and Batch Images to 3D.

### Can I use a negative prompt in Text to 3D?

Yes. Add exclusions such as "no background elements" or "no text or labels" to remove unwanted features.

---

## Next steps
- To write prompts that produce better models, see [Prompting best practices](/webapp/guides/prompting).

- To add color and materials to your model, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To generate from a reference image instead, see [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d).

---

# AI Texturing
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing

# AI Texturing

Generate PBR textures for a 3D model from a text prompt or a reference image, whether Meshy generated the model or you uploaded it.

Use AI Texturing to texture an untextured mesh, to replace textures you aren't happy with, to change a model's material style, or to get a complete PBR texture set. To touch up one area of a texture instead, use [Texture Edit](/webapp/guides/texture-edit). To paint textures by hand, export the model with its UVs and work in a tool such as Substance Painter. For color or brightness adjustments only, use your DCC tool.

---

## Before you begin
You need a model in your generations. To texture a model you made in another tool, upload it first:

1. In the panel that lists your generations, click **Upload**.

2. Add a `.fbx`, `.obj`, `.stl`, `.gltf`, or `.glb` file up to 100 MB.

3. Click **Continue**.

---

## Texture a model
To texture a model, follow these steps:

1. In the panel that lists your generations, click the model.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Texture**. If the model already has textures, the button is **Retexture**.

3. In the panel, select **Text Input** to describe the material, or **Image Input** to match a reference image.

4. If the panel shows a model list, select **Meshy 7 - Flagship** for the most detail, **Meshy 6**, or **Meshy 6 Lite** for the fastest result.

5. Describe the material or add the image:

   - With **Text Input**, describe the material in **Prompt** in up to 800 characters, for example "rusted iron with scratches".

   - With **Image Input**, add a `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, or `.webp` image up to 20 MB. With Meshy 7 - Flagship, you can also turn on **Multi-view** to add images from other angles. Multi-view needs a paid plan.

6. Optional: If the panel shows **Generate PBR Maps**, turn it on to get metallic, roughness, and normal maps in addition to the base color.

7. Optional: If the panel shows **Texture Resolution**, select **2K**, **4K**, or **8K**. 4K and 8K need a paid plan, and 8K is available with Meshy 7 - Flagship only.

8. Optional: With Meshy 6, turn on **Remove Lighting** to remove highlights and shadows from the base color.

9. Click **Texture**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you start. Texturing costs 10 credits, or 15 credits at 8K.

10. Optional: To check the textures under different lighting, switch the viewer to its PBR preview mode, and then change the HDRI in the environment settings.

11. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download** to export the model with its textures.

![Meshy AI Texturing panel: texture a model from a text or image prompt, with Remove Lighting, PBR maps, and HD Texture options](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/ai-texturing-p0-1-1.png)

---

## Settings and tradeoffs
The following table shows what each setting trades off.

| Setting | Options | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI model | Meshy 7 - Flagship, Meshy 6, or Meshy 6 Lite | Meshy 7 - Flagship gives the most detail and the sharpest textures, in about 2 to 3 minutes. Meshy 6 takes about a minute. Meshy 6 Lite is the fastest, at about 30 seconds, and always generates at 2K. |
| Remove Lighting | On or off | On removes baked highlights and shadows, which suits PBR pipelines. Off keeps the original lighting. Available with Meshy 6 at 2K or 4K. |
| Generate PBR Maps | On or off | On adds metallic, roughness, and normal maps to the base color for a complete PBR set. Off gives the base color only. |
| Texture Resolution | 2K, 4K, or 8K | 2K generates faster. 4K gives more detail. 8K gives the most detail and costs 15 credits instead of 10. |
| Prompt | Free text | A more specific prompt gives better results. Combine several style keywords. |

---

## Examples
A specific prompt with the right settings gives a complete texture set:

- Input: a low-poly sword mesh with no textures, and the prompt "ancient elvish blade, silver with blue rune engravings, fantasy style"

- Settings: Meshy 6 with **Remove Lighting** and **Generate PBR Maps** on, at a resolution that suits your use

- Result: a complete PBR texture set with detailed engravings and an accurate metallic look.

A one-word prompt on a mesh with poor UVs gives a poor result:

- Input: a dense mesh with overlapping UVs, and the prompt "wood"

- Result: visible texture seams and distortion.

- Fix: run Unwrap UV to generate a clean UV layout, and then texture the model again.

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Texture seams are visible | The UV layout is poor | Run [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv), and then texture the model again. |
| The PBR maps look flat | Baked shadows stay in the texture | Use Meshy 7 - Flagship, which removes baked lighting automatically, or select Meshy 6 and turn on **Remove Lighting**. |
| The texture style doesn't match the prompt | The prompt is too short | Add details about the material, era, wear level, and colors. |
| Textures load slowly | 4K and 8K texture files are large | If you don't need a high resolution, select **2K**. |
| Meshy says the model has too many faces to texture | The model has 8 million faces or more | Reduce the face count with [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh). Meshy opens the Remesh panel for you. |

---

## FAQ
### How do I add textures to a 3D model in Meshy?

Select a model or upload your own, and click Texture in the viewer toolbar. Enter a material prompt or add a reference image, and then click Texture in the panel.

### Can I texture a model I made elsewhere?

Yes. Upload a .fbx, .obj, .stl, .gltf, or .glb file up to 100 MB, and texture it like a model that Meshy generated.

### What does Remove Lighting do?

It removes baked-in highlights and shadows from the base color texture, so PBR rendering looks correct under any lighting. It's available with Meshy 6.

### What PBR maps does Meshy generate?

With Generate PBR Maps turned on, Meshy generates metallic, roughness, and normal maps in addition to the base color. You can generate at 2K or 4K, or at 8K with Meshy 7 - Flagship.

### Why do my textures have seams or distortion?

Poor UVs usually cause this. Run Unwrap UV to generate a clean UV layout, and then texture the model again.

---

## Next steps
- To generate clean UVs before you texture a model, see [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv).

- To optimize the mesh before you texture it, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

- To fix one area of a texture without replacing it, see [Texture Edit](/webapp/guides/texture-edit).

---

# Auto Split
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/auto-split

# Auto Split

Split a 3D model into watertight parts that you print separately and assemble, for oversized models, figures, and multi-color prints.

If the model already fits your printer's build volume and prints cleanly in one piece, you don't need to split it. For exact cut positions or custom joints, cut the model by hand in a tool such as Blender or Meshmixer.

---

## Before you begin
- Split needs a paid plan.

- You need an untextured model that you generated in Meshy with **High Detail** and Meshy 6 or Meshy 7.1. Textured, uploaded, and remeshed models can't be split, and neither can Meshy 6 Lite or Smart Topology models.

---

## Split a model
You can split a model when you generate it. In Image to 3D with Meshy 6 or Meshy 7.1, or in Text to 3D with Meshy 6, turn on **Split** before you click **Generate**. **Split** needs **Texture** turned off and adds 10 credits. The toggle has no settings, so to choose how the model splits, split it after generation instead.

To split a model after generation, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Print**.

2. In the list of your generations, select an untextured model.

3. Under **Post-Processing**, click **Split**.

4. Select a mode:

   - **Custom**: The default. Under **Split Plan**, select **By Parts** to split the model into structural parts, or **By Color** to split it by the colors of the reference image. **By Color** is available only for models generated from an image. Meshy suggests a description of the parts, which you can edit to name up to 10 parts.

   - **Auto**: Meshy splits the model without a description.

5. Optional: Turn on **Connectors** to add a connector at each cut surface. Select **Cube** or **Cylinder**, and adjust **Size** and **Height**.

6. Click **Split**. The panel shows the cost, 10 credits, and the estimated time. **Custom** takes about 1 minute, and **Auto** about 10 seconds, or 20 seconds with **Connectors** on.

When the split finishes, the split result shows each part in a different color.

---

## Check the parts
To check how the parts fit together, do any of the following:

- Drag the slider in the split toolbar to pull the parts apart, and drag it back to bring them together.

- Select **Assembled** to see the parts fitted together, or **On Plate** to see them laid out flat on the print plate.

- Click **Parts** to list every part with its color and number. To hide or show a part, click the eye icon in its row.

- To try a different split, click **Re-split** in the toolbar, and then click **Re-split** in the panel. Meshy splits the original model again and saves the result as another version. Your current parts stay saved, and each re-split costs credits.

---

## Download the parts
To download the parts, follow these steps:

1. In the split toolbar, select **Assembled** to export the parts in their fitted positions, or **On Plate** to export them laid out for printing, ready to import into your slicer without repositioning.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download**.

3. In **Download Settings**, under **Format**, select a format:

   - 3MF: Keeps each part separate with its own filament color, up to 16 colors.

   - GLB or OBJ: Keeps each part and its color.

   - STL: Exports one mesh, without separate parts or colors.

4. Click **Download**.

To open the parts in a slicer such as Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer instead, in the **Print** panel, under **Send to Printer**, select your slicer. **Send to Printer** needs a Pro plan or higher.

---

## Example
  <iframe
className="w-full h-full rounded-2xl"
src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/fy322el7aDo"
title="Meshy Auto Split walkthrough"
frameBorder="0"

allowFullScreen

---

## Tips
- Models with clear, separable structures give the best results. Good candidates are characters without many small accessories or tangled surface details, multi-part props, landmark miniatures, and figurines with distinct bases.

- Models with windows or openings, dense tangled details such as chains, hair, or mesh patterns, and highly abstract shapes are harder to split cleanly.

---

## FAQ
### Can the split parts be exported with colors for multi-color printing?

Yes. Download the parts as 3MF, and each part gets its own filament slot in its color, up to 16 colors. GLB and OBJ also keep the part colors, and STL exports one mesh without colors. To split the model along the colors of its reference image, set Split Plan to By Color.

### Why did my model split badly or fail?

Auto Split works best on models with clear, separable structures, like character figurines with distinct limbs. Models with dense tangled details, such as chains, hair strands, or mesh patterns, and very abstract shapes are harder to split cleanly. Try Re-split, or switch between the Auto and Custom modes.

### How is Auto Split different from the planar cut tool in my slicer?

A planar cut slices the model along a flat plane, which leaves straight seams across surfaces. Auto Split cuts along the shapes of the model's parts, so the seams follow the structure and the assembled model shows fewer visible gaps.

### Can I auto-split a model I made or uploaded elsewhere?

No. Auto Split works on untextured models generated in Meshy with High Detail and Meshy 6 or Meshy 7.1.

---

## Next steps
- To print the parts, see [3D printing workflow](/webapp/guides/use-cases/3d-printing).

- To generate a model that you can split, see [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d).

# Batch Images to 3D
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/batch-images-to-3d

# Batch Images to 3D

Turn up to 10 images into 10 separate 3D models in one run, when you need a set of assets such as game props or product models.

Batch Images to 3D offers the High Detail and Smart Topology models listed in the following steps, without the Multi-view, Split, and Texture options. To turn a single image into a model, or several photos of the same object into one model, use [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d). To generate a set of concepts in a consistent style through a chat, use [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

---

## Before you begin
- Batch Images to 3D needs a paid plan.

- Each image must be a `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, or `.webp` file of up to 20 MB.

---

## Generate models from several images
To generate models from several images, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Model**.

2. At the top of the panel, click the **Batch Images to 3D** tab.

3. Select **High Detail** for a detailed mesh, or **Smart Topology** for fewer polygons and cleaner topology.

4. In the model list, select an AI model. **High Detail** offers **Meshy 7.1 - Flagship**, **Meshy 6**, and **Meshy 6 Lite**. **Smart Topology** offers **Meshy T2** and **Meshy T1**.

5. In **Images**, add up to 10 images. Click the upload area, drag the files onto it, or paste an image. The label shows how many images you've added, for example 6/10.

6. Optional: Set the options. They apply to every image in the batch:

   - **Resolution**: With Meshy 7.1, select **Standard**, **Ultra 2K**, or **Ultra 4K**.

   - **Pose**: Select **A-Pose** or **T-Pose** for characters you plan to rig.

   - **Image Enhancement**: On by default with Meshy 7.1 and Meshy 6. Meshy redraws each image for a cleaner, more complete model. Turn it off to keep the details of polished artwork.

7. Click **Batch Generate**. The panel shows the cost before you generate, as the credits per image times the number of images.

Meshy starts one generation for each image. Each model appears in the list of your generations, where you can select it to check it in the viewer.

![Meshy Batch Images to 3D: six character images uploaded at once, batch-generated into 3D models in a single queue](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/batch-images-to-3d-p1-1.webp)

---

## Download the models together
To download several models in one file, follow these steps:

1. At the top of the list of your generations, click **Multi-select**. Multi-select needs a Pro plan or higher.

2. Select up to 10 models.

3. Click **Download**.

4. In **Download Settings**, select a format, and then click **Download**.

---

## FAQ
### How do I convert multiple images to 3D at once?

In the left sidebar, click Model, and then click the Batch Images to 3D tab. Add up to 10 images, choose the settings, and click Batch Generate.

### When should I use Batch Images to 3D?

Use it when you have several images, up to 10 per batch, that should each become a separate model, such as a set of game props or product photos.

### Can I set different parameters per image in a batch?

No. The settings you choose apply to every image in the batch. To use different settings for one image, generate it in Image to 3D.

### How is batch processing different from single Image to 3D?

Batch Images to 3D starts one generation for each image in a single step. It offers High Detail with Meshy 7.1, Meshy 6, and Meshy 6 Lite, and Smart Topology with Meshy T2 and Meshy T1, but not Multi-view, Split, or Texture.

### Can I download all batch results together?

Yes. In the list of your generations, click Multi-select, select up to 10 models, and click Download.

---

## Next steps
- To add color and materials to the models, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To generate a single model with Multi-view, Split, or Texture, see [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d).

# Remesh
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh

# Remesh

Rebuild a model's mesh with a target polycount and cleaner topology to make an AI-generated model ready for production.

AI-generated models often have too many triangles and irregular topology. Remesh a model when its face count is too high for your platform, such as over 50,000 faces for a game or over 10,000 for mobile. Remesh also gives cleaner topology for [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv) and [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging). Skip it when the model already has a good face count and topology. While you explore concepts, remesh only the final model.

---

## Remesh a model
To remesh a model, follow these steps:

1. In the panel that lists your generations, click the model.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Remesh**. If a menu opens, select **Remesh**.

3. Under **Target Polycount**, select **Fixed** to set the face count yourself, or **Adaptive** to let Meshy set it from the model's structure.

4. Select a target. On a free plan, only **10K** is available, and the other targets need a paid plan.

   - With **Fixed**, select **3K**, **10K**, **30K**, or **100K**. To set another value from 100 to 300,000, select **Custom**.

   - With **Adaptive**, select **Low**, **Medium**, **High**, or **Ultra**.

5. Under **Topology**, select **Quad** or **Triangle**. Quad gives evenly spaced faces that are easier to edit, with less detail at a given face count. Triangle keeps more detail at a given face count and suits game engines, but it's harder to edit.

6. Click **Confirm**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you start. Remesh costs no credits and takes about a minute.

7. When Meshy finishes, compare the remeshed model with the original to check that the details you need are kept.

Meshy saves the remeshed model as a separate model in your generations and keeps the original.

![Meshy Remesh settings: choose a fixed or adaptive target polycount and quad or triangle topology before regenerating the mesh](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/remesh-p0-1.webp)

---

## Settings and tradeoffs
The following table shows how the target face count trades detail for performance and file size.

| Target faces | Use case | Detail loss | File size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Under 5,000 | Mobile AR, casual games | Noticeable | Small |
| 5,000 to 20,000 | Mobile games, web viewers | Minor | Medium |
| 20,000 to 50,000 | PC and console games | Minimal | Medium |
| 50,000 to 100,000 | High-quality renders | Very low | Large |
| Over 100,000 | Film and cinematic work | Negligible | Very large |

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The model loses too much detail | The target face count is too low | Raise the target face count until you find the balance between quality and performance. |
| The mesh has holes after remeshing | The original mesh has non-manifold edges | Remesh at a higher face count, or repair the original mesh first. |
| Small accessories disappear | The face budget is spread unevenly across the model | Remesh complex models one part at a time. |
| The **Remesh** button is missing | Remesh doesn't support Meshy T2 models or split parts | Regenerate a Meshy T2 model at the face count you need. Remesh other models before you split them. |

---

## FAQ
### What does Remesh do in Meshy?

Remesh rebuilds a model's topology and sets its face count, so an AI-generated mesh is ready for production.

### How many polygons should a game model have?

Aim for under about 50,000 faces for PC games and under about 10,000 for mobile games. Set the target in Target Polycount in the Remesh panel.

### Do I need to Remesh before 3D printing?

No. To make a mesh watertight for 3D printing, click Make Printable in the Printability card in the viewer. Remesh changes the face count and topology.

### Will Remesh reduce my model's detail?

A lower target trades some detail for performance. Compare the original and remeshed models, and raise the target if you need more detail.

### When should I Remesh in my workflow?

Remesh the final model before UV unwrapping, texturing, or rigging. Skip it while you explore concepts.

---

## Next steps
- To retexture the remeshed model for better results, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To generate UVs for the remeshed model, see [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv).

- To rig a model that has clean topology, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

---

# Rigging
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging

# Rigging

Add a skeleton to a humanoid or four-legged character so you can animate it in Meshy or in engines such as Unity and Unreal.

For a custom skeleton, such as facial bones or tail physics, download the model and rig it by hand in a DCC tool such as Blender or Maya.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a character model in the list of your generations. It can be a model you generated in Meshy, or a `.fbx`, `.obj`, `.stl`, `.gltf`, or `.glb` file of up to 100 MB that you added with **Upload**. The model doesn't need textures.

- For the best result, the character stands in a T-pose or A-pose, with a clear gap between the limbs and the body. To generate a character in that pose, set **Pose** to **A-Pose** or **T-Pose** in [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) or [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d).

- If a generated model has more than 300,000 faces, Meshy asks you to reduce the face count with [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) before rigging.

---

## Rig a character
To rig a character, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Animate**.

2. In the list of your generations, select the character.

3. In the viewer toolbar, click **Rig**. The **Rig Model** dialog opens.

4. Under **Select Character Type**, select the type that matches your character:

   - **Humanoid**: A character with two arms and two legs.

   - **Quadruped Dog**: A four-legged character.

   - **Smart Rig (Beta)**: Any other model, such as a creature, robot, or prop. Meshy rigs it automatically, without markers, so click **Confirm** and skip the remaining steps. Smart Rig models can't use the animation library and download as GLB only.

5. Click **Next**.

6. Use **Rotate**, **Offset**, and **Height** to center the character, turn it to face the front, and set its height in meters. Turn a four-legged character to face the left side of the screen. **Offset** is for humanoids only.

7. Click **Next**. For a humanoid, Meshy places markers on the joints automatically.

8. Drag each marker onto its body part. For a humanoid, the markers are the chin, shoulders, elbows, wrists, groin, knees, and ankles. With **Symmetry** on, which is the default for humanoids, Meshy mirrors each marker you move to the other side.

9. Click **Confirm**. On the Free and Starter plans, the button is **Generate**.

When rigging finishes, a humanoid comes with walking and running animations, and a four-legged character with a walking animation. To add more, see [Animation](/webapp/guides/animate).

![Meshy Rig Model panel: place body markers like chin, shoulders, and knees on the character, with symmetry enabled for precise auto-rigging](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/rigging-p0-1.webp)

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rigging fails with a message that the markers aren't positioned correctly | One or more markers are outside the model | Click **Re-rig** and place every marker on the body. |
| Bones are in the wrong place | The model isn't close to a T-pose or A-pose | Generate the character with **Pose** set to **A-Pose** or **T-Pose**, and then rig it again. |
| The mesh clips through itself when the character moves | The topology is too dense or uneven | Use [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) to reduce the face count, and then rig the remeshed model. |
| Limbs deform badly | The character's proportions are far from a standard body | Use a character with proportions close to a standard human body. |

---

## FAQ
### How do I rig a 3D character in Meshy?

In the left sidebar, click Animate, select the character, and click Rig. Choose the character type, adjust the model, place the markers on its joints, and click Confirm.

### What models can Meshy auto-rig?

Humanoid and four-legged characters, rigged with markers that you place. Smart Rig rigs other models, such as creatures, robots, and props, without markers, but Smart Rig models can't use the animation library.

### Is Meshy rigging compatible with Unity and Unreal?

Yes. Download the rigged model as FBX or GLB. For a humanoid, Download Settings also lets you choose a skeleton template, such as Mixamo, which is the default.

### Should I Remesh before rigging?

Yes. Clean topology gives the most accurate bone binding and weight assignment, so Remesh first. A generated model with more than 300,000 faces must be remeshed before you can rig it.

### Can I rig a model for facial expressions or tail physics?

Not in Meshy. For a custom skeleton, download the model and rig it by hand in a DCC tool such as Blender or Maya.

---

## Next steps
- To add motion to the rigged character, see [Animation](/webapp/guides/animate).

- To clean up the topology before rigging, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

---

# Unwrap UV
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv

# Unwrap UV

Generate a clean UV layout automatically to prepare a model for AI Texturing or for texturing by hand.

UV quality directly affects texture results, and a good layout has no seams and no stretching. Run Unwrap UV after [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) and before [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing), when an imported model has no UVs, or when AI Texturing shows visible seams. Skip it if your model already has good UVs from a DCC tool, or if you only need geometry, such as an STL file for 3D printing. Unwrap UV isn't available on mobile.

---

## Unwrap a model's UVs
To unwrap a model's UVs, follow these steps:

1. In the panel that lists your generations, click the model.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Remesh**, and then select **Unwrap UV**. For a model that can't be remeshed, such as a Meshy T2 model, click **Unwrap UV** in the viewer toolbar instead.

3. In the **Unwrap UV** dialog, click **Confirm**. Unwrap UV costs 5 credits. If the model has quad topology, the dialog tells you that Unwrap UV converts it to triangle topology.

4. When Meshy finishes, in the panel that lists your generations, click the unwrapped model. Meshy saves it as a separate model and keeps the original.

5. Optional: In the viewer, click **View UV**, and check the UV islands in **UV Layout** for stretching. To see the seams on the model, turn on **3D Seams**. To spot stretching, turn on **UV Checker**.

You can then texture the unwrapped model with [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A Remesh panel opens instead of the **Unwrap UV** dialog | The model has more faces than Unwrap UV supports. The panel shows the limit. | In the panel, set **Target Polycount**, and then click **Remesh**. When Meshy finishes, run Unwrap UV on the remeshed model. |
| Meshy says the model has too many faces to unwrap | The model has more faces than Unwrap UV supports, and it can't be remeshed | Regenerate the model at a lower face count, and then run Unwrap UV. |

---

## FAQ
### What does Unwrap UV do?

It generates a clean UV layout automatically. It unwraps your 3D surface into 2D space so textures apply without seams or stretching.

### When should I use Unwrap UV?

Use it after Remesh, when an imported model has no UVs, or when AI Texturing shows visible seams.

### Do I need to Unwrap UV before AI Texturing?

It's recommended. Good UVs are the foundation for clean textures without seams.

### Do I need Unwrap UV after Remesh?

Not to keep your textures, because Remesh bakes them onto the new mesh. Run Unwrap UV after Remesh when you want a clean UV layout for texturing by hand or for AI Texturing.

### When can I skip UV unwrapping?

Skip it if your model already has good UVs, or if you only need geometry, for example an STL file for 3D printing.

---

## Next steps
- To texture the unwrapped model, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To rebuild the topology before you unwrap a model, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

---

# Animation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/animate

# Animation

Rig a character and add motions from a library of more than 600 presets, then download it as FBX, GLB, or USDZ for Unity, Unreal, or Blender.

For motion the library doesn't cover, download the rigged FBX and animate it by hand in Blender or Maya, or retarget Mixamo animations. Detailed cinematic animation with facial expressions also needs a tool such as Maya or Blender.

---

## Animate a character
To animate a character, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Animate**.

2. In the list of your generations, select a character model. A character in a T-pose or A-pose gives the most accurate rig.

3. If the model isn't rigged, click **Rig** and complete the **Rig Model** dialog. For the full rigging flow, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

4. In the **Library** tab, find a motion. Enter a name in **Search motion**, or open **Category** and select **Walk & Run**, **Daily Actions**, **Dancing**, **Fighting**, or **Body Movements**.

5. On the motion's card, click **Add**. Meshy applies the motion, and you can click the card to preview it in the viewer.

6. Optional: Add more motions. Every motion you add appears in the **Added** tab.

7. Optional: To create a motion that isn't in the library, at the top of the **Library** tab, click **Text to Motion**, and then describe the motion.

A few motions are available on every plan, and the rest need a paid plan. Adding a preset costs no credits. **Text to Motion** costs credits. Four-legged characters come with a walking animation, and the preset library and **Text to Motion** are for humanoid characters.

![Meshy Animate module: browse the animation preset library and apply clips like dances and gestures to a rigged character](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/animation-p0-1.webp)

---

## Download the animated model
To download the animated model, follow these steps:

1. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download**.

2. In **Download Settings**, under **Format**, select FBX, GLB, or USDZ.

3. Optional: Choose what to include. For example, with FBX or GLB, under **Animation**, select **Current** for the motion that's playing or **All Added** for every motion you added. For a humanoid, you can also select a **Skeleton template**, such as **Mixamo**, which is the default.

4. Click **Download**.

---

## Tips
- Generate characters in a T-pose or A-pose for the most accurate rig. In Image to 3D and Text to 3D, set **Pose** to **A-Pose** or **T-Pose**.

- For animations beyond the library, download the rigged FBX, and then retarget Mixamo clips or create your own keyframes in Blender's Action Editor.

---

## FAQ
### How do I animate a 3D character in Meshy?

In the left sidebar, click Animate, and select the character. Rig it if it isn't rigged, add motions from the library, preview them in the viewer, and download the result.

### How many animation presets does Meshy have?

More than 600 presets for humanoid characters, in five categories: Walk & Run, Daily Actions, Dancing, Fighting, and Body Movements.

### Can I animate a model I made outside Meshy?

Yes. Upload the model to the list of your generations, and then rig and animate it. A model in a T-pose or A-pose works best.

### What formats can I export animated models in?

FBX, GLB, or USDZ. FBX includes the skeleton and animation data and works with Unity, Unreal, and Blender.

### Can I create custom animations not in the library?

Yes. Use Text to Motion to generate a motion from a description for a humanoid character. You can also download the rigged FBX, and then create keyframes or retarget Mixamo clips in Blender or Maya.

---

## Next steps
- To set up the skeleton before you animate, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

- To bring an animated model into Blender, see [Animated Models](/webapp/plugins/blender/animated-models).

# Choose a generation method
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/generation-method

# Choose a generation method

Compare Text to 3D, Image to 3D, Multi-view, and 3D Agent to pick the generation method that fits your input, the precision you need, and how you like to work.

No single method is best for every project. The right choice depends on what you start from, how closely the model must match a reference, and how much creative guidance you want.

---

## Compare the methods
The following table compares the four methods. The ratings are relative to each other.

| Factor | Text to 3D | Image to 3D | Multi-view | 3D Agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference images | None | 1 image | 2 to 4 images | Optional |
| Precision | Medium | High | Highest | Medium |
| Speed | High | High | Medium | Medium |
| Creative freedom | Highest | Medium | Low | Highest |
| Consistency across generations | Low | High | Highest | High |
| Back-side accuracy | Medium | Medium | Highest | Medium |
| Batch production | Yes | Yes, with Batch Images to 3D | Limited, because each model needs its own set of views | Yes, in a conversation |
| Guided creative process | No | No | No | Yes |
| Answers to 3D creation questions | No | No | No | Yes |

---

## When to choose each method
Choose Text to 3D when:

- You're exploring and want to try several directions.

- You have no reference image, only an idea.

- You want to control the style and material through the prompt.

Choose Image to 3D when:

- You have a concept image, product photo, or sketch.

- You need the result to match a reference image closely.

- You're turning product photos into 3D models for e-commerce.

Choose Multi-view when:

- You have images of the same object from several sides.

- You need an accurate model from every side.

- You're digitizing a physical product.

Multi-view is an option in Image to 3D with Meshy 7.1. When you turn on **Multi-view**, you can add a left, back, and right view to the main image.

Choose 3D Agent when:

- You want help deciding what to create.

- You need a batch of concepts in one consistent style, for example a set of game props.

- You know how to 3D print but not how to model.

- You want to ask questions about 3D creation or printing as you work.

---

## FAQ
### Should I use Text to 3D or Image to 3D?

Use Text to 3D to explore concepts when you have no reference. Use Image to 3D when you have a photo or sketch and need the model to match it.

### What is Multi-view best for?

Multi-view suits high-fidelity reconstruction when you have images of the same object from several sides, such as when you digitize a product. Turn it on in Image to 3D with Meshy 7.1, and add up to 3 views to the main image.

### When should I use 3D Agent instead?

Use 3D Agent when you want help deciding what to create, need a batch of concepts in one style, or prefer a guided conversation.

### Which Meshy method is most accurate?

Image to 3D and Multi-view give the most precise results because they work from real visual references.

### Is there one best 3D generation method?

No. The right choice depends on your input, how precise the model must be, and how much creative guidance you want.

---

## Next steps
- To generate a model from a written description, see [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d).

- To generate a model from one or more images, see [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d).

- To create a model through a conversation, see [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

# Choose the web app, 3D Agent, or API
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/integration

# Choose the web app, 3D Agent, or API

Compare the Meshy web app, 3D Agent, and the API to choose whether you create 3D models in a UI, through a conversation, or fully automated from your own code.

The web app suits individuals and small teams who want to work in a UI without code. 3D Agent suits brainstorming, guided creation, and makers without modeling experience. The API suits automation, batch processing, and building 3D generation into your own product.

---

## Comparison
The following table compares the three ways to work with Meshy.

| Factor | Web app | 3D Agent | API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Learning curve | Low, no coding needed | Low, you chat with the agent | Medium, you write code |
| Automation | No | Limited | Full |
| Batch processing | Limited, with Batch Images to 3D | Yes, in a conversation | Yes, at scale |
| Integration with other tools | No | No | Yes, with your own systems |
| Real-time preview | Yes | Yes | No, you build your own |
| Brainstorming | No | Yes | No |
| Best for | Individuals and designers | Makers and creators | Developers and teams |

---

## FAQ
### Should I use the Meshy web app, 3D Agent, or API?

Use the web app to create in a UI, 3D Agent to create through a guided conversation, and the API to automate generation and integrate it with your own systems.

### Does the Meshy web app require coding?

No. You work in the web app entirely through its UI, which suits individuals and small teams.

### When should I use the Meshy API?

Use the API to automate generation, process large batches, and build 3D generation into your own product or pipeline.

### Who is 3D Agent for?

3D Agent is for makers and creators who want to brainstorm, get guided creation, and make batches in one style without modeling experience.

### Can I switch between the web app, 3D Agent, and API?

Yes. They share the same Meshy account and models, so you can move between them as your needs change.

# Choose a post-processing step
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/post-processing

# Choose a post-processing step

Decide when to use Remesh, AI Texturing, Unwrap UV, or Rigging on a generated model, and in which order, so the asset is clean and ready to export.

---

## Decide what your model needs
After you generate a model, check what it needs:

- If the face count is too high or the topology is messy, use [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

- If you plan to 3D print the model, click **Make Printable** in the **Printability** card in the viewer to make the mesh watertight. For more information, see [3D printing workflow](/webapp/guides/use-cases/3d-printing).

- If the texture quality isn't good enough, you want a different style, or you need PBR maps, use [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing). If seams are still visible after texturing, use [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv), and then run AI Texturing again.

- If you plan to hand-paint the textures, use Unwrap UV.

- If a character needs animation, remesh it first for clean topology, then rig it with [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging), and then animate it.

- If none of these apply, the model is ready to export.

When a model needs several of these tools, use them in this order:

1. Remesh

2. Unwrap UV

3. AI Texturing

4. Rigging

5. Animate

After the last step, export the model.

---

## FAQ
### When should I remesh a model?

Remesh when the face count is too high or the topology is messy. To make a mesh watertight for 3D printing, click Make Printable in the Printability card in the viewer instead.

### When should I retexture a model with AI Texturing?

Use AI Texturing when the texture quality isn't good enough, you want a different style, or you need a full set of PBR maps.

### When do I need Unwrap UV?

Use Unwrap UV when textures show visible seams or you plan to hand-paint textures in a DCC tool.

### When should I rig a model?

Rig a character when you want to animate it. Remesh it first to clean up the topology.

### What's the right order for post-processing?

Remesh first, then use Unwrap UV, AI Texturing, Rigging, and Animate. Export the model last.

---

## Next steps
- To lower the face count or clean up the topology, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

- To regenerate textures or add PBR maps, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To prepare a character for animation, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

# AI image generation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/image/ai-image-generation

# AI image generation

Generate 2D images from a text prompt and turn the one you like into a 3D model, so you control the look before you generate in 3D.

Generating an image first gives you more control over the visual style than [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d), which goes straight from text to a model. If you already have a reference image, use [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) directly. To brainstorm and explore concepts in a chat, use [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

---

## Generate an image and turn it into 3D
To generate an image and turn it into a 3D model, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Image**.

2. In **AI Model**, select a model. Each model has its own cost, from 3 to 12 credits per image.

3. In **Prompt**, describe the image in up to 800 characters, for example "a low-poly cartoon fox sitting, front view, white background". You can write the prompt in your own language.

4. In **Number of images**, select how many images to generate, from 1 to 8. On the Free and Starter plans, you can generate up to 4 images a day.

5. Optional: Adjust the other settings:

   - **Refine Prompt**: Meshy refines your prompt for 3D generation by default, with clearer structure, defined angles, and simpler backgrounds. This can make the style more cartoonish. To use your prompt as written, click the wand icon in the prompt box to turn it off.

   - **Image References**: Add up to 5 images to guide the result.

   - **Styles**: Select a preset style, such as **Japanese Anime**, **Western Realism**, or **Chibi Blind Box**. **Styles** is available with the **Nano Banana Pro** and **Nano Banana 2** models. When you select a style, **Multi-view** and **Pose** turn off.

   - **Aspect Ratio**: Select the image shape. The default is 1:1.

   - **Multi-view**: Turn on to generate consistent front, side, and back views.

   - **Pose**: Select **A-Pose** or **T-Pose** for a character you plan to rig.

6. Click **Generate**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you generate.

7. In the list of generated images, hover over the one you want to use.

8. Optional: To change the 3D generation settings, click the settings icon next to **Image to 3D**.

9. Click **Image to 3D**. Meshy starts generating a 3D model from the image and opens the **Image to 3D** tab in **Model**.

![Meshy AI Image Generation workspace: text prompts produce 3D-ready concept images like low-poly foxes and wizard characters, with aspect ratio and stylization controls](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/ai-image-generation-p1-1.webp)

---

## Prompt tips for 3D-ready images
These tips help the image convert cleanly to 3D:

- Ask for a "front view" or "3/4 view", which are the best angles for 3D conversion.

- Add "white background" or "clean background" so the background doesn't interfere.

- Describe the complete form. Describe the entire object, not only the head.

- Avoid complex scenes. A single subject converts best.

---

## FAQ
### How do I generate an image from text in Meshy?

In the left sidebar, click Image, enter a prompt, and click Generate. To turn an image into a 3D model, hover over it and click Image to 3D.

### What's the difference between AI image generation and Text to 3D?

AI image generation creates a 2D image first, which gives you more control over the look before you convert it to 3D. Text to 3D goes straight from text to a model.

### How do I write prompts for 3D-ready images?

Ask for a front or 3/4 view and a white background, describe the whole object, and keep to a single subject.

### What image styles can Meshy generate?

Preset styles include Japanese Anime, Western Realism, and Chibi Blind Box. Styles are available with the Nano Banana Pro and Nano Banana 2 models.

### Can I send a generated image directly to Image to 3D?

Yes. Hover over the image and click Image to 3D. Meshy starts generating a 3D model from that image.

---

# Assets
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/platform/asset-management

# Assets

Find, organize, and download every model you generate in Meshy or upload from another tool.

Meshy saves each generation to **Assets** automatically. While you work, the list next to the viewer shows the same generations. Each post-processing step, such as texturing or remeshing, saves its result as a new asset and keeps the original, so you can go back to an earlier version.

![Meshy My Assets view: browse and filter models by type, texture, and animation status, with batch selection and upload](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/my-models-asset-management-p1-1.webp)

---

## Find a model
To find a model, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Assets**. **My Assets** opens with your **Models**. To see your images instead, click **Images**.

2. In the search box, enter a word from the model's name or prompt.

3. Optional: To narrow the list, click **All**, **Model**, **Textured**, or **Animation**.

4. Optional: Click **Filter** to filter by status, label, source, geometry, and more.

5. Click the model to open it in the viewer.

To see each generation together with the assets made from it, switch the layout to **List View** at the bottom of the list. Click a group to see all of its assets.

Each model card has a menu with actions such as **Rename**, **Add Label**, **Download**, and **Delete**. You can add up to 20 labels to a model and create up to 100 labels in total.

---

## Act on several models at once
Batch actions need a Pro plan or higher. To download, label, or delete several models at once, follow these steps:

1. In **My Assets**, click **Batch Selection**.

2. Select the models. You can download up to 10 models at a time.

3. Click **Download**, **Add Label**, or **Delete**.

4. If you clicked **Download**, select a format in **Download Settings**, and then click **Download**.

5. Click **Done** to leave batch selection.

---

## Upload a model
To texture, remesh, or otherwise post-process a model you made in another tool, upload it to Meshy:

1. In **My Assets**, click **Upload**.

2. Drag your file onto the upload area, or click the area to select it. Meshy accepts `.fbx`, `.obj`, `.stl`, `.gltf`, and `.glb` files up to 100 MB.

3. In **Model Name**, enter a name for the model.

4. Optional: Turn on **Keep Original Texture and UV** to keep the model's own texture and UV map.

5. Click **Continue**.

The uploaded model appears in your assets, and you can post-process it like a model you generated.

---

## FAQ
### Where are my generated models stored in Meshy?

Meshy saves every generation automatically. Click Assets in the left sidebar to search, filter, and act on your models.

### Can I upload my own models to Meshy?

Yes. Upload an FBX, OBJ, STL, glTF, or GLB file up to 100 MB, then post-process it with tools such as AI Texturing and Remesh.

### Can I see previous versions of a model?

Yes. Each post-processing step saves a new asset and keeps the original. In the list view of Assets, Meshy groups each generation with the assets made from it.

### How do I download multiple models at once?

In Assets, click Batch Selection, select up to 10 models, and click Download. Batch actions need a Pro plan or higher.

### Why can't I download my model?

Check that the generation finished. If Meshy says you've reached your download limit, upgrade your plan to download more models.

# Export and file formats
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/platform/export-formats

# Export and file formats

Pick the file format that fits where your model goes next, whether that's a game engine, a 3D tool, AR, the web, or a 3D printer.

Meshy exports eight formats: GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, STL, BLEND, 3MF, and DXF. Animated models download as FBX, GLB, or USDZ. GLB embeds textures in one file, while FBX and OBJ use separate texture files.

---

## Choose a format
The following table shows which format to use for each common task.

| I need to... | Format | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Display a 3D model on a web page | GLB | Web standard, embedded textures, small size |
| Import into Unity | FBX | Best native Unity support, and it keeps your rig |
| Import into Unreal Engine | FBX | Best native Unreal support, and it keeps your rig |
| Import into Blender | BLEND, GLB, or FBX | BLEND opens as a Blender file. GLB and FBX import too, and GLB is the more open format. |
| View in Apple AR Quick Look | USDZ | The AR format for Apple devices |
| 3D print in a single color | STL | Every slicer supports it |
| 3D print in color | 3MF from Multi-Color Print or a split model | A regular 3MF download has geometry only. For color, export from **Multi-Color Print** in the **Print** panel, or download split parts. |
| Open the mesh in CAD software | DXF | Stores the mesh as faces that CAD tools read |
| Exchange with older DCC tools | OBJ | Widest compatibility, but limited features |

---

## Download a model
To download a model in the format you chose, follow these steps:

1. In the list of your generations, select the model.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download**.

3. Optional: In **Download Settings**, turn on **Resize** to set the model's real-world size. Enter the **Height**, select a unit, and under **Origin**, select **Bottom** or **Center**. **Resize** needs a paid plan.

4. In **Format**, select the format.

5. Click **Download**.

---

## FAQ
### What 3D file formats does Meshy export?

GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, STL, BLEND, 3MF, and DXF. Together they cover games, AR, 3D printing, CAD, and DCC tools.

### Which format should I use for game engines?

Use FBX for Unity and Unreal. GLB is best for the web and AR.

### Which format should I use for 3D printing?

Use STL or 3MF for single-color prints. For color prints, export 3MF from Multi-Color Print in the Print panel, or download split parts as 3MF.

### How does Meshy handle textures in each format?

GLB embeds textures in one file, while FBX and OBJ use separate texture files that you must keep together.

### Why does my model appear white (no textures) after import?

The textures probably weren't linked. Reassign the texture maps in your engine, or export GLB, which embeds them.

---

# Prompting best practices
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/prompting

# Prompting best practices

Write prompts that produce better 3D models, using a four-part formula, tips for each goal, and examples of good and bad prompts.

---

## Prompt structure formula
An effective prompt combines four parts:

```text
[Subject] + [Material/Texture] + [Art Style] + [Technical Constraints]
```

For example, this prompt uses all four parts:

```text
A medieval knight's helmet with scratched iron surface in dark fantasy art style, low-poly, game-ready asset
```

The prompt breaks down into these parts:

- Subject: "A medieval knight's helmet"

- Material: "with scratched iron surface"

- Style: "in dark fantasy art style"

- Technical constraints: "low-poly, game-ready asset"

A longer prompt isn't always better. Put the most important details first, because the first words carry the most weight. A Text to 3D prompt can be up to 800 characters.

---

## Prompt tips by goal
Different goals need different prompts.

For realistic models:

- Describe real materials, for example "brushed stainless steel" or "oak wood with visible grain".

- Add detail in layers: the main body first, then surface details, then wear and aging.

- Avoid descriptions that contradict each other.

For stylized or cartoon models:

- Name the style, for example "Pixar style", "Studio Ghibli", or "flat shading cel-shaded".

- Describe the shape language, for example "round", "exaggerated proportions", or "chibi".

For game assets:

- Select **Smart Topology** as the model type, and add "game-ready" to the prompt.

- Avoid long descriptions of fine detail.

- Include "clean edges" and "minimal geometry".

For 3D printing:

- Ask for a sturdy structure with words such as "solid", "watertight", and "no floating parts".

- Avoid very thin features.

- Specify "printable proportions".

For 3D Agent conversations:

- Write as you would in a conversation. The agent uses your earlier messages as context.

- Start broad ("I want to create cyberpunk props for a game"), and let the agent help you refine the idea.

- Ask for several concepts at once, for example "Show me 6 variations of this idea".

- Refer to earlier concepts, for example "I like the third one. Can we make it more detailed?"

---

## Prompt dos and don'ts
The following table pairs prompts that work with prompts that don't.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| "a wooden treasure chest with iron bands" | "a box" (too vague) |
| "front-facing, centered, white background" | "stunning beautiful epic" (empty adjectives) |
| "low-poly cartoon style, 5,000 faces" | "make it look good" (not actionable) |
| "weathered stone surface with moss" | "stone and wood and metal and glass" (too many materials) |

---

## Negative prompts
To exclude unwanted elements, add a negative phrase to the prompt. For example:

- "no background elements"

- "without floating particles"

- "no text or labels"

---

## Good and bad examples
A specific prompt names the subject, materials, style, and technical constraints:

- Good: "A sci-fi plasma rifle with glowing blue energy core, carbon fiber body with chrome accents, cyberpunk style, game-ready low-poly asset"

- Bad: "cool gun"

A prompt for 3D printing also gives structural guidance:

- Good: "A chess rook piece, medieval castle tower design, solid structure, no thin overhangs, 8 cm tall, printable without supports"

- Bad: "chess piece", which gives no structural guidance for printing

---

## FAQ
### How do I write a good 3D generation prompt?

Use the formula Subject + Material/Texture + Art Style + Technical Constraints, and put the most important details first.

### Do longer prompts produce better 3D models?

Not necessarily. Clarity and key details placed first matter more than length, because the first words carry the most weight.

### How do I prompt for low-poly game assets?

Select Smart Topology as the model type, include "low-poly" or "game-ready" in the prompt, add "clean edges" and "minimal geometry," and avoid heavy detail.

### How do I prompt for 3D-printable models?

Emphasize "solid," "watertight," and "no thin overhangs," avoid very thin features, and specify printable proportions.

### Can I use negative prompts in Meshy?

Yes. Exclude unwanted elements with phrases such as "no background elements," "without floating particles," or "no text or labels."

---

# 3D scenes
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/scene-video/scene-compose

# 3D scenes

Arrange several 3D models into one scene by moving, rotating, and scaling them, for game level prototypes, architecture visualization, or product showcases.

In **Scene**, you can also render an image of the scene and send it to Video. To make a single standalone object, generate it in [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) or [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d) instead. For professional scene editing, export your models to a tool such as Blender or Unity.

---

## Compose a scene
To compose a scene, follow these steps:

1. From the Meshy home page, in the left sidebar, point to **Create**, and then click **Scene**. Meshy opens your most recent scene and the **3D Scenes** list.

2. In **3D Scenes**, click **Create Scene**, or select a scene to keep working on.

3. On the **Model** tab, click a model to add it to the scene. The **Community** tab adds models from the Meshy community.

4. In the viewport, select an object and drag its handles to move, rotate, or scale it.

5. Optional: For exact values, in **Panel > Object**, set **Position**, **Rotation**, and **Scale**.

6. Optional: In **Panel > Camera**, set the **Position**, **Rotation**, and **Field of View**, or click **Frame All** to fit every object in view.

7. Optional: In **Panel > Scene**, adjust the **Environment** lighting and the **Ground**.

Meshy saves the scene automatically. The header shows **Saved** when your changes are stored.

---

## Render an image of the scene
To turn the scene into an image, follow these steps:

1. In **Image Render**, enter a **Prompt** that describes how the scene should look.

2. Optional: Select a **Model** and a **Resolution**.

3. Click **Generate**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you generate.

4. Optional: To animate the result, click **Send to Video** on the image in **Image Generation**.

---

## FAQ
### What can I do with 3D scenes in Meshy?

Place several 3D models in one scene, move, rotate, and scale them, and render an image of the scene from a camera you set.

### What are 3D scenes best for?

Game level prototypes, architecture visualization, and product showcase scenes built from several assets.

### Can I generate a video from a scene?

Yes. Render an image of the scene in Image Render, then click Send to Video on the image to animate it in Video.

### When should I not use a 3D scene?

To make a single standalone object, generate it in Image to 3D or Text to 3D. For professional scene editing, export your models to Blender or Unity.

### Can I export a scene layout to a game engine?

No. Meshy keeps the scene in the web app. To rebuild it in a game engine, export each model, for example through the Meshy plugins, and arrange the models there.

---

## Next steps
- To animate an image of your scene, see [AI video generation](/webapp/guides/scene-video/video-generation).

- To bring your models into Blender, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

# AI video generation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/scene-video/video-generation

# AI video generation

Generate a short video from an image or a text prompt, for product showcases, social media content, and project demos.

To show off a 3D model, place it in a scene with [3D scenes](/webapp/guides/scene-video/scene-compose), render an image of it, and send the image to Video. For complex cinematic rendering, export your model to Blender, Arnold, or another professional renderer instead.

<YouTube id="n4sT-Rb7LjU" title="3D to Video: A New Way to Create Your Vision in Meshy" />

---

## Create a video
To create a video, follow these steps:

1. From the Meshy home page, in the left sidebar, point to **Create**, and then click **Video**. If you clicked **Send to Video** in a scene, Video opens with that image already added.

2. In **Create Video**, click **Image to Video** or **Text to Video**.

3. For **Image to Video**, add an image in **Image**. Video generation needs a paid plan.

4. In **Prompt**, describe the scene and how it moves.

5. Select a **Model**, and then set the options the model offers. **Image to Video** shows **Duration**, **Quality**, and **Audio Generation**. **Text to Video** shows **Duration**, **Aspect Ratio**, and **Audio Generation**.

6. Click **Generate**. The panel shows the time and credit cost before you generate.

The video appears in the list of your videos. Select it to play it.

---

## FAQ
### How do I create a video from a 3D model in Meshy?

Place the model in a 3D scene, render an image of it in Image Render, and click Send to Video. In Video, describe the motion, choose a model, and click Generate.

### What can I customize in AI video generation?

The prompt, the AI model, and, depending on the model, the duration, the quality, and whether to generate audio.

### What is AI video generation best for?

Product showcase videos, social media content, and project demos of your 3D models.

### When should I not use Meshy for video?

For cinematic-grade rendering, export your model to Blender, Arnold, or another professional renderer.

### Do I need to compose a scene before generating a video?

No. You can upload any image in Image to Video, or start from a prompt in Text to Video. A 3D scene lets you control the camera and lighting of the image you animate.

# Texture Edit
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/texture-edit

# Texture Edit

Fix or change one area of a model's texture by painting directly on the 3D model, with a real-time preview.

Use Texture Edit when AI Texturing gives a good overall result but some areas need work, such as a misplaced pattern, color bleed, or seam artifacts. You can also add or change a detail on one part of the model, for example battle damage on one shoulder or a different logo on a chest plate. To replace the whole texture from a fresh prompt, use [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing). To change the mesh shape, click **Edit** in the viewer toolbar, or edit the model in Blender with [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

---

## Before you begin
You need the following:

- A model with textures. To add textures first, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- A computer. Texture Edit isn't available on mobile.

- A paid plan to save your edits to the model.

---

## Key features
The following table describes the tools in the texture editor.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **AI Texture Edit** | Draw a mask on the area you want to change, enter a prompt that describes the result, and click **Retexture**. You can also add a reference image. Works from any camera angle. |
| **Healing Tool**, in **Brush Tool** | Paint over imperfections, such as seams, artifacts, and color bleed, while you orbit the model. The tool fills and blends the repaired area automatically. |
| **Stamp Tool**, in **Brush Tool** | Copy texture from one spot of the model and paint it onto another. |
| **Solid Paint Tool**, in **Brush Tool** | Paint a color you pick directly onto the model. |
| **Decal Tool** | Upload an image and click the model where you want to place it. You can set its width, height, rotation, and opacity. |
| **History** | Lists every edit. Select an earlier entry to go back to that version. |

---

## Edit a texture
To edit a texture, follow these steps:

1. In the panel that lists your generations, click a textured model.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **Edit Texture**. The texture editor opens.

3. In the editor toolbar, click **Free Camera Mode**, and rotate the view to the area you want to change. While another tool is active, you can hold Space to move the camera.

4. Change the area with one of these tools:

   - To regenerate the area, click **AI Texture Edit**, draw a mask over the area, describe the look you want in **Prompt**, and click **Retexture**.

   - To heal an imperfection, click **Brush Tool**, select **Healing Tool**, and paint over the artifact or seam. The tool blends the area automatically.

   - To place an image, click **Decal Tool**, upload the image, and click the model where you want it.

5. In **History**, select the result you want, and click **Apply**.

6. Repeat from other angles as needed. To compare versions, select earlier entries in **History**.

7. Click **Save to Model**. If you close the editor before you save, you lose your changes.

<YouTube id="SZeBC_g_ARg" title="New Decal Tool is LIVE! | 3D Texture Editing Just Got Smarter" />

---

## Tips
- Work from several angles so your edits blend across UV seams.

- Use AI Texture Edit for creative changes, such as adding details or changing the style. Use the Healing Tool for corrections, such as removing artifacts or smoothing seams.

- Generate the base texture with AI Texturing, and then refine specific areas with Texture Edit.

---

## FAQ
### How do I edit a 3D model's texture in Meshy?

Open a textured model and click Edit Texture. Orbit to the area, mask the region with AI Texture Edit, and enter a prompt to regenerate it with a real-time preview.

### Can I fix texture artifacts without regenerating everything?

Yes. The Healing Tool blends out seams and imperfections in the areas you paint and leaves the rest of the texture unchanged.

### When should I use Texture Edit instead of AI Texturing?

Use Texture Edit for local touch-ups and detail changes. Use AI Texturing to regenerate the entire surface from a different prompt.

### Can I undo texture edits?

Yes. Texture Edit keeps every edit in History. Select an earlier entry to compare versions or go back to one.

### Can I edit textures from any angle?

Yes. Orbit the model and paint or regenerate from several angles so your edits blend across UV seams.

---

## Next steps
- To regenerate the whole texture from a prompt, see [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing).

- To generate a textured model from one image, see [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d).

# 3D printing workflow
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/use-cases/3d-printing

# 3D printing workflow

Take a Meshy model from generation to a file your slicer can print, for miniatures, figurines, chess pieces, custom gifts, decorations, or prototypes.

Meshy can generate print-ready models, but they need some post-processing first. A model prints well when its mesh is watertight, its walls are thick enough for your printer, and you export it in the right format. To brainstorm a custom model through a chat before you generate, use [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

---

## Prepare a model for printing
To prepare a model for printing, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Model**.

2. Generate the model in Text to 3D or Image to 3D with **High Detail** selected. In a Text to 3D prompt, add "solid, printable, no thin overhangs". To print from an image, use Meshy 7.1 in [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d). It handles lettering and shallow relief well, which saves you modeling them by hand.

3. In the left sidebar, click **Print**. If the panel asks you to select a model, select it in the list of your generations.

4. In the viewer, check the **Printability** card. For details, such as whether the mesh is **Watertight** and how many **Holes** and **Non-manifold edges** it has, click **Print Check**.

5. If the card shows issues, click **Make Printable**. The repair fixes non-manifold edges, degenerate faces, holes, and open boundaries so the mesh is watertight, and it thickens walls that are too thin. It costs 10 credits, and for a model that Meshy generated, it needs a paid plan. Repairing a textured model discards its texture, so texture it again afterward.

6. Optional: In the **Print** panel, under **Post-Processing**, click **Add Base** to add a stable base, or **Split** to split the model into parts.

7. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download**.

8. In **Download Settings**, turn on **Resize**, and then enter the printed **Height**. The unit is cm by default, and you can switch to mm, m, in, or ft. **Resize** needs a paid plan.

9. In **Format**, select STL or 3MF, and then click **Download**. This download has geometry only. For a color print, export from **Multi-Color Print** in the **Print** panel instead, or download split parts as 3MF.

10. Open the file in your slicer, such as OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio, and slice it.

11. Send the sliced file to your 3D printer.

On a Pro plan or higher, you can skip the download. In the **Print** panel, under **Send to Printer**, select your slicer to open the model in it.

<YouTube id="y_wZVIUkiGI" title="AI Auto-Repair: Generate Print-Ready Models in One Click" />

---

## Design for printability
### Minimum wall thickness

The following table shows the thinnest wall each print technology can reliably print.

| Print technology | Minimum wall thickness | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FDM | 1.2 mm | Depends on nozzle diameter |
| SLA or DLP | 0.5 mm | Better for fine details |
| SLS | 0.8 mm | No support needed |

### Overhangs

- FDM: Overhangs steeper than 45° need support.

- SLA: More forgiving of overhangs, but still needs support points.

- SLS: Needs no support, which gives the most design freedom.

### Base and stability

- Add a base to character and figurine models.

- Make the base at least 3 mm thick.

- To get a base from the start, add "with a stable circular base" to your prompt or 3D Agent chat.

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common printing problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The slicer reports a non-manifold mesh | The mesh has open edges or overlapping faces | In the **Printability** card, click **Make Printable**. |
| The print breaks | The connection points are too thin | Thicken the connection areas in a DCC tool. |
| The bottom warps | The base is too thin, or the print doesn't stick to the bed | Thicken the base, and use a brim or raft when you print. |
| Details are lost | The print resolution is too low | Use a higher-precision printer, such as SLA, or scale up the model. |
| Colors look wrong | The 3MF color mapping has issues | Preview and adjust the colors in your slicer. |

---

## Export formats for 3D printing
The following table compares the formats you can use for 3D printing.

| Format | Color | Best for | Slicer support |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| STL | No | FDM or SLA single-color printing | All slicers |
| 3MF | Yes, from Multi-Color Print or split parts | Color and multi-material printing | Cura, PrusaSlicer, and Bambu Studio |
| OBJ | Limited | Limited color support | Some slicers |

---

## FAQ
### Can I 3D print models made with Meshy?

Yes. Generate your model, check its printability, set its size, and export STL or 3MF for your slicer.

### What makes a Meshy model 3D-printable?

A watertight mesh, adequate wall thickness, and the correct export format (STL or 3MF).

### Should I export STL or 3MF for 3D printing?

Use STL or 3MF for single-color printing. For color printing, export 3MF from Multi-Color Print in the Print panel, or download split parts as 3MF.

### How do I fix a model that isn't watertight?

In the Printability card in the viewer, click Make Printable. It fixes non-manifold edges, degenerate faces, and holes so the mesh is watertight.

### What wall thickness and base do figurines need?

Keep walls thick enough for your printer and material, and add a stable base at least 3 mm thick to figurines.

---

## Next steps
- To brainstorm custom printing ideas through a chat, see [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

- To learn what a watertight mesh is, see [Glossary](/webapp/glossary).

- To open models in your slicer from Meshy, see [Meshy 3D Printing Platforms Documentation](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/introduction).
