# Game assets
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/use-cases/game-assets

# Game assets

Generate characters, props, environment objects, and vehicles for your game, and take them through optimization, texturing, rigging, and export.

Meshy suits prototyping, indie game development, placeholder assets, and concept exploration. To build a set of assets that share one art style for a cohesive game world, use [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent). Export FBX for Unity and Unreal, or GLB for the web and Three.js.

---

## Make a game character
To take a game character from generation to export, follow these steps:

1. Generate the base character with Text to 3D, Image to 3D, or 3D Agent.

2. Remesh the character to your polygon budget, for example 5,000 for mobile or 20,000 for PC. In the viewer toolbar, click **Remesh**, and set **Target Polycount**. For details, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

3. Texture the character with PBR maps. In the viewer toolbar, click **Texture**, or **Retexture** if the character already has textures. Turn on **Generate PBR Maps**, and generate the texture. PBR maps add metallic, roughness, and normal maps to the base color.

4. In the viewer toolbar, click **Animate**, and then click **Rig** to auto-rig the character with a humanoid skeleton.

5. In the **Library** tab, browse the more than 600 animation presets, and click **Add** on the motions you want. The library sorts presets into categories such as **Walk & Run**, **Body Movements**, **Daily Actions**, and **Fighting**.

6. In the viewer toolbar, click **Download**, and then in **Format**, select FBX for Unity or Unreal, or GLB for the web.

7. Click **Download**.

<YouTube id="MUJp6wOqu6M" title="Meshy + Blender: How to Create 3D Characters in Dramatic Poses in MINUTES!" />

---

## Make a style-consistent asset set with 3D Agent
To generate a set of assets that share one art style, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar, click **Agent**.

2. In the message box, describe your game's visual direction, for example "I'm building a cyberpunk RPG and need a set of props." The agent suggests creative directions and generates a batch of visual concepts.

3. Select your favorites, ask for variations, and adjust the style through the chat.

4. Ask the agent to turn the concepts you selected into 3D models.

5. Remesh, texture, and download the models as needed.

<YouTube id="00tiy745MAc" title="Generate a Full Set of Game Assets in One Chat with Meshy 3D Agent" />

---

## Polygon budget reference
The following table shows typical polygon budgets for each platform and asset type. Use them as Remesh targets.

| Platform | Character | Prop | Environment piece |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile (casual) | 3,000 to 5,000 | 500 to 2,000 | 1,000 to 5,000 |
| Mobile (AAA) | 10,000 to 20,000 | 2,000 to 5,000 | 5,000 to 15,000 |
| PC or console | 20,000 to 50,000 | 5,000 to 15,000 | 10,000 to 50,000 |
| VR | 10,000 to 30,000 | 2,000 to 8,000 | 5,000 to 20,000 |

---

## FAQ
### Can I use Meshy to make game assets?

Yes. Meshy generates characters, props, environment objects, and vehicles, then optimizes and rigs them for Unity and Unreal.

### What's the workflow for a game-ready character in Meshy?

Generate the character, remesh it to your polygon budget, texture it with PBR maps, rig it, animate it, and export FBX or GLB.

### What polygon budget should I target for games?

Roughly 5,000 polygons for mobile and 20,000 for PC. Use Remesh to hit your target.

### Which export format should I use for Unity or Unreal?

FBX for Unity and Unreal, and GLB for web and Three.js projects.

### How do I make a style-consistent set of game assets?

Use 3D Agent to generate batches of concepts with a shared art direction, then turn them into 3D models.

---

- To set up characters for animation, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

- To generate style-consistent concepts through a chat, see [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent).

# Bambu Studio
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/bambu-studio

# Bambu Studio

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into Bambu Studio, ready to slice for your Bambu Lab printer.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Bambu Studio** opens the upgrade options.

- Install Bambu Studio on the computer where you use the Meshy web app. The web app opens Bambu Studio through your browser, so you don't need a plugin.

## Send a model
To send a model to Bambu Studio, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar of the Meshy web app, click **Print**. If the panel asks you to select a model, select it in the list of your generations.

2. In the **Print** panel, under **Send to Printer**, click **Bambu Studio**.

3. In the browser prompt, select **Always allow www.meshy.ai to open links of this type in the associated app** so the browser doesn't ask again, and then click **Open BambuStudio**.

   ![Browser prompt asking to open BambuStudio, with the Always allow checkbox selected and the Open BambuStudio button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/5.png)

4. When Bambu Studio asks whether to open a file that isn't from a trusted site, click **Yes**.

   ![Bambu Studio message saying the file isn't from a trusted site, with an arrow pointing to Yes](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/6.png)

5. If Bambu Studio opens a dialog saying that the 3MF isn't from Bambu Lab, select **Don't show again**, and then click **OK**.

   ![Bambu Studio message saying the 3MF isn't from Bambu Lab, with Don't show again selected and the OK button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/7.png)

Meshy sends the model as a 3MF file, and Bambu Studio adds it to the build plate, ready to slice.

   ![Bambu Studio Prepare tab with the imported Meshy model on the build plate of a Bambu Lab A1](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/8.png)

You can also send from the viewer toolbar. With the **Print** panel open, click **Send to Printer** (the paper plane icon), and then click **Send to Bambu Studio**.

   ![Meshy web app viewer with a textured model and an arrow pointing to the Print button in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtoprint.webp)

   ![Print menu in the Meshy viewer with an arrow pointing to Send to Bambu Studio](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtobambu.webp)

You can send models from your generations, whichever tool made it.

   ![Print menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Bambu Studio and Send to OrcaSlicer](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc-moreprint.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **Print** (the 3D printer icon), and then click **Send to Bambu Studio**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc-community.webp)

# 3D printing platforms
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/introduction

# 3D printing platforms

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your slicer or printer software, such as Bambu Studio or Ultimaker Cura, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking an app opens the upgrade options.

- Install the app on the computer where you use the Meshy web app. The web app opens the app through your browser, so you don't need a plugin.

## Send a model to your app
To send a model to your app, follow these steps:

1. In the left sidebar of the Meshy web app, click **Print**. If the panel asks you to select a model, select it in the list of your generations.

2. In the **Print** panel, under **Send to Printer**, click your app.

3. In the browser prompt, click the button that opens the app.

Meshy exports the model, and the app opens it. Some apps ask you to confirm the import first. For the steps in your app, see its page in the following table.

You can also send from the viewer toolbar. With the **Print** panel open, click **Send to Printer** (the paper plane icon), and then click your app in the menu.

## Supported platforms
The following table lists the apps you can send models to, and the file format Meshy sends to each.

| App | Description | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Flash Studio](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/flash-studio) | Official slicer for Flashforge 3D printers | 3MF |
| [Snapmaker Orca](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/snapmaker) | Official slicer for Snapmaker 3D printers | 3MF |
| [xTool Studio](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/xtool-studio) | Official software for xTool laser engravers and UV printers | OBJ |
| [Bambu Studio](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/bambu-studio) | Official slicer for Bambu Lab 3D printers | 3MF |
| [OrcaSlicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/orcaslicer) | Open-source slicer based on Bambu Studio | 3MF |
| [Creality Print](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/creality-print) | Official slicer for Creality 3D printers | 3MF |
| [Elegoo Slicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/elegoo-slicer) | Official slicer for Elegoo 3D printers | 3MF |
| [Ultimaker Cura](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/ultimaker-cura) | Official slicer for Ultimaker 3D printers | STL |
| [Lychee Slicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/lychee-slicer) | Slicer by Mango3D for resin and filament 3D printers | STL |

To print a textured model in several colors, click **Multi-Color Print** in the **Print** panel. It can send the multi-color model to every app in the table that gets a 3MF file.

# Lychee Slicer

   ![Save As dialog over Lychee Slicer with the file name Meshy.3mf and its extension highlighted](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_confirm1.webp)

   ![Lychee Slicer Layout view with the imported model on the build plate and the Move panel open](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_lychee_result.webp)

You can send models from your generations, whichever tool made it.

   ![Print menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to LycheeSlicer and other slicers](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_moreprint.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **Print** (the 3D printer icon), and then click **Send to LycheeSlicer**.

# Animated models

## Send an animated model

To send an animated model, follow these steps:

It doesn't import the skin weights from the file, so check how the mesh follows the bones, and re-skin it if needed.

To play the animation, press the Spacebar in the viewport, and then click **Play Animation**.

# Bridge to 3ds Max
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/3dsmax/bridge-to-3ds-max

# Bridge to 3ds Max

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open 3ds Max scene, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to 3ds Max** opens the upgrade options.

- Download and unzip the Meshy plugin for 3ds Max. For the steps, see [Meshy for 3ds Max](/webapp/plugins/3dsmax/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in 3ds Max, follow these steps:

1. If the **Meshy Bridge for 3ds Max** window isn't open, click **Scripting > Run Script**, and then select `3dsmax_meshy_bridge.py`.

2. Click **Run Bridge**. The button changes to **Stop Bridge**, the status changes to "Status: Running", and the plugin waits for models from Meshy.

   ![Meshy Bridge Control panel in 3ds Max with an arrow pointing to the Run Bridge button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/4.PNG)

To stop the bridge, click **Stop Bridge**.

## Send a model
To send a model to 3ds Max, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to 3ds Max**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to 3ds Max](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendto3ds.webp)

Meshy sends the model as an FBX file. The plugin imports it into the open scene, gives its objects names that start with `Meshy_`, and builds a Physical Material from its textures.

   ![3ds Max perspective viewport with the imported woodland model selected and listed in the Scene Explorer](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/9.png)

You can send any model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to 3ds Max and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/newpanel/doc-moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to 3ds Max**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/newpanel/doc-community.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to 3DS Max" | 3ds Max isn't open, the bridge isn't running, another app uses port `5329`, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | In the **Meshy Bridge for 3ds Max** window, click **Run Bridge**, and then send the model again. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy. If the send still fails, close any other app that uses port `5329`. |
| After you click **Run Bridge**, the status stays "Status: Stopped" | Another app uses port `5329`, such as a second 3ds Max session with the bridge on. | Close the other app or stop its bridge, and then click **Run Bridge** again. |

## Next steps
- To bring a rigged character and its animation into 3ds Max, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/3dsmax/animated-models).

# Bridge to Blender
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender

# Bridge to Blender

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open Blender scene, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Blender** opens the upgrade options.

- Install the Meshy plugin in Blender. For the steps, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in Blender, follow these steps:

1. In the 3D viewport, press `N` to open the sidebar.

2. Click the **Meshy** tab.

3. In the **Meshy Bridge** panel, click **Run Bridge**. The button changes to **Bridge ON**, and the plugin waits for models from Meshy on port `5324`.

   ![Meshy Bridge panel in the Blender sidebar with the Run Bridge button and its tooltip, Starts the Meshy Bridge server](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/2.png)

Start the bridge each time you open Blender. To stop it, click **Bridge ON**.

## Send a model
To send a model to Blender, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to Blender**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to Blender](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc_sendtoblender.webp)

Meshy sends the model as a GLB file, and the plugin imports it into the open scene.

   ![Model in the Meshy web app next to the same model imported into the Blender viewport, with Bridge ON in the Meshy Bridge panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v052/29.webp)

> **Note:** If the imported model looks plain gray, the viewport is in **Solid** shading, which doesn't show textures. The import still worked. To see the materials, hover over the 3D viewport, press `Z`, and select **Material Preview**. You can also use the shading buttons in the viewport header.
>
> ![Blender shading pie menu with Material Preview circled, next to the imported model's material settings](/images/blender-plugin/material-preview-z.png)

You can send any model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Blender and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc-moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Blender**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc-community.webp)

## How the bridge works
The bridge is a local server that the plugin runs inside Blender. When you click **Send to Blender**, the following happens:

1. The web app checks that the bridge is running at `http://localhost:5324/status`, and then sends the model's download URL to `http://localhost:5324/import`.

2. The plugin downloads the file to a temporary folder. You can keep working in Blender while it downloads.

3. The plugin checks whether the file is a GLB file or a ZIP file.

4. The plugin imports the model with the Blender glTF importer, and merges duplicate vertices.

5. The plugin renames the imported object to `Meshy_`, then the model name, then the object's original name. If the mesh has no material, the plugin adds one that shows its vertex colors.

6. The plugin deletes the temporary files.

## Supported file formats
The bridge imports these file types:

- **GLB**: Meshy sends a static model as a GLB file.

- **ZIP**: Meshy sends an animated model as a ZIP file. The plugin extracts it and imports the first GLB file inside.

The glTF importer brings in the model's materials, textures, and vertex colors, and the armature and animation of an animated model.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to blender" | Blender isn't open, the bridge isn't running, another app uses port `5324`, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | Open Blender. In the **Meshy Bridge** panel, click **Run Bridge**, and then send the model again. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy. If the send still fails, close any other app that uses port `5324`. |
| The panel shows **Bridge ON**, but Meshy shows "Failed to send model to blender" | Pressing `Esc` in Blender stops the bridge, and the button keeps showing **Bridge ON**. | Click **Bridge ON**, click **Run Bridge**, and then send the model again. |

## Next steps
- To bring a rigged character and its animation into Blender, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/blender/animated-models).

- To check an imported model for 3D printing problems, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

# Meshy for Blender
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction

# Meshy for Blender

Install the Meshy plugin in Blender so you can send models from the Meshy web app into your scene and prepare them for 3D printing.

---

## Before you begin
- Download the plugin, a `.zip` file, from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/blender"}>Meshy for Blender integration page</ExternalLink>. Don't unzip it. Blender installs the plugin from the `.zip` file.

- You need Blender 4.2 or later.

- You need a Meshy account. To send models with the bridge, you need a Pro plan or higher.

Meshy tested the plugin with Blender 4.2.6, 5.0.1, 5.1.0, and 5.2.0.

The plugin doesn't need an API key or a sign-in. You generate and texture models in the Meshy web app, and the plugin receives them in Blender.

## Install the plugin
To install the plugin, follow these steps:

1. In Blender, click **Edit > Preferences**.

2. In the **Preferences** window, click **Add-ons**.

3. At the top of the add-on list, click the drop-down arrow.

4. Click **Install from Disk**.

   ![Blender Preferences window on Add-ons, with the drop-down menu open and Install from Disk highlighted](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v050/2.png)

5. In **Blender File View**, select the `.zip` file you downloaded.

6. Click **Install from Disk**.

   ![Blender File View with the Meshy plugin zip file selected, Enable on Install checked, and the Install from Disk button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v050/3.png)

7. In the add-on list, search for `Meshy`.

8. Make sure the plugin's checkbox is selected.

9. In the 3D viewport, press `N` to open the sidebar. You can also click the small arrow at the edge of the viewport.

   ![Blender 3D viewport with a red box around the small arrow that opens the sidebar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/panel-entrance.webp)

10. Click the **Meshy** tab.

![Blender sidebar with the Meshy tab open, showing the Meshy Bridge panel and its Run Bridge button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/1.png)

You can also install the plugin by dragging the `.zip` file into the Blender viewport.

## Plugin panels
The **Meshy** tab has the **Meshy Bridge** panel and four panels that prepare a model for 3D printing. Its **Help & Settings** panel opens the plugin's user guide in English or Chinese.

### Bridge to Blender

**Meshy Bridge** receives the models you send from the Meshy web app and imports them into the open scene, with their materials and vertex colors. To set it up, see [Bridge to Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender).

### Model analysis
**Analyze** measures volume and surface area. It also checks the mesh for problems that make a 3D print fail, such as holes, self-intersections, thin walls, and overhangs. To run the checks, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

### Model cleanup
**Clean Up** repairs the mesh with **Make Manifold**, which fills holes, deletes loose and interior geometry, and makes the normals point outward. Its **Delete Small Pieces** tool removes scattered fragments. To repair a model, see [Model cleanup](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup).

### Model editing
**Edit** hollows a model, rotates it so chosen faces sit flat with **Align XY**, and scales it to a target volume or length. To change a model, see [Model editing](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-editing).

### Model export
**Export** saves the selected objects as STL, OBJ, or PLY files, with options for UVs, normals, vertex colors, and textures. To export a model, see [Model export](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export).

## Prepare a model for 3D printing
To prepare a model for 3D printing, follow these steps:

1. Send the model from Meshy to Blender with **Meshy Bridge**.

2. In the **Analyze** panel, click **Check All** to find problems.

3. In the **Clean Up** panel, fix the problems.

4. In the **Edit** panel, set the model's size and orientation.

5. In the **Analyze** panel, click **Check All** again to confirm the fixes.

6. In the **Export** panel, export the model as an STL file.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The sidebar has no **Meshy** tab | The plugin is installed but turned off. | In **Edit > Preferences > Add-ons**, search for `Meshy`, and select the plugin's checkbox. |
| The **Meshy** tab shows **Meshy Login** or **Text To Texture** | An older version of the plugin is installed. | Download the plugin from the Meshy for Blender integration page, and install it again. |

- To send your first model from Meshy to Blender, see [Bridge to Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender).

- To check a model for 3D printing problems, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

- To import a rigged character with its animation, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/blender/animated-models).

# Model analysis
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis

# Model analysis

Check a model in Blender for problems that make 3D prints fail, such as holes, thin walls, and overhangs, with the **Analyze** panel of the Meshy plugin.

---

## Before you begin
- Install the Meshy plugin in Blender. For the steps, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

## Check a model
To check a model, follow these steps:

1. Click the model to make it the active object. If you select several objects, the checks evaluate only the active one.

2. In the 3D viewport, press `N` to open the sidebar.

3. Click the **Meshy** tab.

4. Expand the **Analyze** panel.

   ![Analyze panel in the Meshy tab with the Statistics and Checks buttons, their default values, Small Pieces, and Check All](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-panel.png)

5. Click **Check All**. To run a single check instead, click its button under **Checks**.

The results appear under **Result**, with the number of problems that each check found. **Check All** runs every check under **Checks**. It doesn't run **Small Pieces**, so run that check on its own.

## Select problem geometry
In Edit Mode, each result that found problems becomes a button that selects the faces, edges, or vertices it found.

To select problem geometry, follow these steps:

1. Press `Tab` to switch to Edit Mode.

   ![Blender in Edit Mode with the Result list in the Analyze panel, where checks that found problems show as buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-results.png)

2. Under **Result**, click a result, such as **Intersect Face**. The plugin selects the geometry that the check found.

   ![Anvil model in Edit Mode with its self-intersecting faces selected after a click on Intersect Face in the Result list](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-selected-geometry.png)

3. Fix or delete the selected geometry.

To clear the results, click the X icon next to **Result**.

## Statistics
Under **Statistics**, click **Volume** or **Area** to measure the active mesh, with its modifiers applied. The value appears under **Result**, in the scene's units, such as m³ or m².

### Volume

Measures the volume of the mesh. Use it to estimate how much material a print needs, to compare model sizes, or to check a size requirement.

### Area

Measures the surface area of the mesh. Use it to estimate paint or coating, or to plan the surface finish.

## Geometry checks
Each button under **Checks**, and the **Small Pieces** button, runs one check on the active mesh. A value next to a button sets that check's limit.

### Solid

Checks that the model is a closed solid with consistent normals. It reports two counts:

- **Non-manifold Edges**: edges that don't join exactly two faces, which point to holes or badly connected geometry.

- **Bad Contiguous Edges**: edges between faces that point in opposite directions, one inward and one outward.

A model must be manifold, or watertight, to print. Slicers can fail on non-manifold geometry.

### Intersections

Finds faces where the model cuts through itself, and reports them as **Intersect Face**. Self-intersections can make a print or a slicer fail, and they throw off measurements such as volume.

### Degenerate

Finds geometry too small to keep:

- **Zero Faces**: faces with an area at or below the square of the limit.

- **Zero Edges**: edges no longer than the limit, where vertices overlap or almost overlap.

Set the limit in the field next to **Degenerate**. The plugin reads the value in centimeters, whatever unit the field shows, so the default `0.01` means 0.01 cm (0.1 mm).

### Non-Planar

Finds faces that aren't flat, and reports them as **Non-flat Faces**. Non-flat faces can cause rendering artifacts and printing problems. Set the angle limit next to **Non-Planar**. The default is 5°.

### Thickness

Finds walls thinner than the value next to **Thickness**, and reports them as **Thin Faces**. The default is 1 mm. Thin walls can break during printing or fail to print.

### Sharp

Finds edges sharper than the angle next to **Sharp**, and reports them as **Sharp Edge**. The default is 160°. Very sharp edges are hard to print accurately and can need support material.

### Overhang

Finds faces that overhang past the angle next to **Overhang**, and reports them as **Overhang Face**. The default is 45°. Large overhangs need support material to print.

### Small Pieces

Finds small loose pieces, such as scattered fragments in a photogrammetry scan or droplets in a fluid simulation.

To find small pieces, follow these steps:

1. Under **Small Pieces**, select how to measure each piece:

   - **Volume**: the volume of the piece's bounding box, in cm³.

   - **Surface Area**: the piece's surface area, in cm².

   - **Diagonal**: the length of the piece's bounding box diagonal, in cm.

2. In the field next to the measure, enter the size limit. The default is `1`. The plugin reads it in cm³, cm², or cm for the selected measure, whatever unit the field shows.

3. Click **Small Pieces**.

The results show how many pieces are smaller than the limit, and the total number of pieces. The **Clean Up** panel uses the same measure and limit to delete small pieces.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The **Analyze** panel is grayed out | The active object isn't a mesh. | Click a mesh object to make it active. |
| Blender shows "Report is out of date, re-run check" | The mesh changed after the check ran. | Run the check again, and then click the result. |

## Next steps
- To fix the problems the checks find, see [Model cleanup](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup).

- To export the model after it passes the checks, see [Model export](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export).

# Model cleanup
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup

# Model cleanup

Repair holes, loose geometry, and flipped normals in Blender, and remove small fragments, with the **Clean Up** panel of the Meshy plugin.

---

## Before you begin
- Install the Meshy plugin in Blender. For the steps, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

- Find the problems first with the checks in the **Analyze** panel. For the steps, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

- Save your Blender file. Both tools change the mesh. You can undo them with `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS).

## Make Manifold
**Make Manifold** repairs a mesh so it's closed and watertight, as a model must be to print.

To run Make Manifold, follow these steps:

1. Select the model.

2. In the **Meshy** tab, expand the **Clean Up** panel.

3. Click **Make Manifold**.

   ![Clean Up panel with Make Manifold highlighted, and the Make Manifold panel in the viewport showing Merge Distance and Sides](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/cleanup-panel.png)

4. Optional: In the **Make Manifold** panel that Blender opens in the viewport, change a setting. Blender runs the repair again with the new value.

   - **Merge Distance**: how close two vertices must be to merge. The default is `0.0001`.

   - **Sides**: the most sides a hole can have to be filled. The default, `0`, fills every hole.

Make Manifold runs these repairs in order:

1. Deletes loose vertices, edges, and faces.

2. Deletes interior faces, which sit inside the model.

3. Merges vertices that are closer than **Merge Distance**.

4. Fills holes, and deletes the non-manifold vertices that filling leaves behind, until the mesh stops changing.

5. Makes all normals point outward.

When it finishes, Blender shows how many vertices, edges, and faces it added or removed.

   ![Blender status bar showing the Make Manifold report, Modified: -3 vertices, -3 edges, -1 faces](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/cleanup-results.png)

Check the result in the viewport, and run **Check All** in the **Analyze** panel again to confirm the fixes.

## Delete Small Pieces
**Delete Small Pieces** deletes loose pieces that are smaller than a limit, such as debris in a photogrammetry scan or droplets in a fluid simulation mesh.

To delete small pieces, follow these steps:

1. Optional: In the **Analyze** panel, run the **Small Pieces** check to see what the tool deletes. The check uses the same measure and limit.

2. Click the model to make it the active object.

3. If the object's scale isn't `1`, apply it with **Object > Apply > Scale**. The **Small Pieces** check measures the scaled model, but **Delete Small Pieces** measures the mesh before scaling, so the two match only when the scale is applied.

4. In the **Clean Up** panel, under **Delete Small Pieces**, select how to measure each piece:

   - **Volume**: the volume of the piece's bounding box, in cm³. Use it to remove small solid fragments.

   - **Surface Area**: the piece's surface area, in cm². Use it to remove thin flakes or sheets.

   - **Diagonal**: the length of the piece's bounding box diagonal, in cm. It works for fragments of any shape.

5. In the field next to the measure, enter the size limit. The default is `1`. The plugin reads it in cm³, cm², or cm for the selected measure, whatever unit the field shows.

6. Click **Delete Small Pieces**.

Blender shows how many pieces the tool deleted. Start with a small limit, and raise it if fragments remain. After the tool runs, check that it didn't remove parts you need.

## Clean up a model for printing
A model is ready to print when it's manifold, has no self-intersections, has the right scale, and has walls thick enough to print.

To clean up a model for printing, follow these steps:

1. In the **Analyze** panel, click **Check All**, and review the results.

2. In the **Clean Up** panel, click **Make Manifold**.

3. If the model has small fragments, click **Delete Small Pieces**.

4. In the **Analyze** panel, click **Check All** again, and confirm that the problems are gone.

5. In Edit Mode, fix any remaining problems by hand.

When all checks pass, export the model from the **Export** panel.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The **Clean Up** panel is grayed out | The active object isn't a mesh. | Click a mesh object to make it active. |
| Blender shows "No small pieces found below threshold" | No piece is smaller than the limit in the selected measure. | Raise the limit. The plugin reads it in cm³, cm², or cm, whatever unit the field shows. |

## Next steps
- To scale, orient, or hollow the repaired model, see [Model editing](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-editing).

- To export the model for printing, see [Model export](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export).

---

# Model editing
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-editing

# Model editing

Hollow, orient, and scale a model in Blender for 3D printing with the **Edit** panel of the Meshy plugin.

---

## Before you begin
- Install the Meshy plugin in Blender. For the steps, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

- Save your Blender file before you make large changes. You can undo each edit with `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS).

## Hollow
**Hollow** builds an offset surface inside or outside a model. With **Hollow Duplicate** selected, it creates a hollow copy of the model. A hollow model uses less material to print, and suits shells for casting, lighter models, and containers or vases.

**Hollow** needs a closed, watertight mesh. If the model has holes, run **Make Manifold** first. For the steps, see [Model cleanup](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup). To check that the walls are thick enough, run the **Thickness** check in the **Analyze** panel.

To hollow a model, follow these steps:

1. Select the model.

2. In the **Meshy** tab, expand the **Edit** panel.

3. Click **Hollow**. The **Hollow** dialog opens.

   ![Edit panel with Hollow highlighted, and the Hollow dialog showing Offset Direction, Offset, Voxel Size, and Hollow Duplicate](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/edit-panel.png)

4. Set the options:

   - **Offset Direction**: **Inside** builds the offset surface inside the model, and **Outside** builds it outside. The default is **Inside**.

   - **Offset**: the wall thickness, the distance between the model's surface and the offset surface. The default is `1.0`, in the scene's length unit, so 1 m in a default scene. With **Inside**, it must be less than half the model's thickness. Start with a small value, and raise it if needed.

   - **Voxel Size**: the size of the voxels the plugin uses to build the surface. Smaller values, such as `0.1` to `0.5`, keep fine detail but take longer. Larger values, such as `1.0` to `2.0`, process faster. The default is `1.0`, in the scene's length unit.

   - **Hollow Duplicate**: whether to also create a hollow copy of the model. It's off by default.

5. Click **OK**.

The plugin adds the result as a new object and keeps the original model unchanged:

- Without **Hollow Duplicate**, the new object holds only the offset surface. It's named after the model, such as `Cube offset`.

- With **Hollow Duplicate**, the new object joins the model's surface and the offset surface into a hollow shell. It's named after the model, such as `Cube hollow`.

To change the options after you click **OK**, use the **Hollow** panel that Blender opens in the viewport.

   ![Cube with its new offset surface inside it, and the Hollow panel in the viewport with the Inside and Outside options](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/hollow-dialog.png)

## Align XY
**Align XY** rotates an object so the faces you select face down, parallel to the XY plane. Use it to make a model sit flat on the print bed.

To align a model, follow these steps:

1. Select the model.

2. Press `Tab` to switch to Edit Mode.

3. Select the faces that should touch the print bed, usually the bottom faces.

4. In the **Edit** panel, click **Align XY**.

   ![Anvil model in Edit Mode with a bottom face selected, Align XY highlighted, and Weight by Face Area checked](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/align-xy-before-after.png)

The plugin rotates the model so the selected faces are parallel to the XY plane.

**Weight by Face Area** gives larger faces more influence on the rotation. It's selected by default, and it gives more stable results on models with faces of different sizes. To clear it, use the **Align XY** panel that Blender opens in the viewport.

To align several objects at once, select them all. Each object needs selected faces, or the plugin skips it.

## Scale to Volume
**Scale to Volume** scales the selected objects evenly until their volume matches a value you enter. Use it to meet a size requirement, match the volume of another model, or plan how much material a print uses.

To scale a model to a volume, follow these steps:

1. Make sure Blender is in Object Mode. In Edit Mode, the tool measures the whole mesh but scales only the selected geometry. To switch modes, press `Tab`.

2. Select the model. If you select several mesh objects, the plugin uses their combined volume.

3. In the **Edit** panel, under **Scale To**, click **Volume**. A dialog opens with the current volume in **Volume**.

4. Enter the volume you want.

5. Click **OK**.

The plugin scales the objects by the same factor on every axis, and Blender shows the scale factor.

## Scale to Bounds
**Scale to Bounds** scales the selected objects evenly so their longest side matches a length you enter. Use it to fit a model on your printer's bed or to meet a size limit.

To scale a model to a length, follow these steps:

1. Make sure Blender is in Object Mode. In Edit Mode, the tool measures the whole mesh but scales only the selected geometry. To switch modes, press `Tab`.

2. Select the model. If you select several mesh objects, the plugin measures them together.

3. In the **Edit** panel, under **Scale To**, click **Bounds**. A dialog opens with the current longest side in **Length**.

4. Enter the length you want, such as the size of your print bed.

5. Click **OK**.

The plugin keeps the model's proportions, and Blender shows the scale factor and the axis of the longest side.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hollow** shows "Make sure target mesh has closed surface and offset value is less than half of target thickness" | The mesh has holes, or **Offset** is too large for the model's thickness. | Run **Make Manifold** in the **Clean Up** panel, or lower **Offset**, and then click **Hollow** again. |
| **Align XY** shows `Skipping object <name>. No faces selected`, with the object's name | An object has no selected faces, so the plugin skips it. | In Edit Mode, select the faces that should face down, and then click **Align XY** again. |

## Next steps
- To export the edited model for printing, see [Model export](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export).

- To check the model again after you edit it, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

---

# Model export
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export

# Model export

Export models from Blender as STL, OBJ, or PLY files for a slicer or other 3D software, with the **Export** panel of the Meshy plugin.

---

## Before you begin
- Install the Meshy plugin in Blender. For the steps, see [Meshy for Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction).

- Get the model ready. Check it in the **Analyze** panel, fix it in the **Clean Up** panel, and set its size and orientation in the **Edit** panel. For the steps, see [Model analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis).

## Export a model
To export a model, follow these steps:

1. Select the objects you want to export. The plugin exports only the selected objects, with their modifiers applied.

2. In the **Meshy** tab, expand the **Export** panel.

3. In the folder field, enter the folder to save the file in, or click the folder icon to browse.

4. In **Format**, select **STL**, **OBJ**, or **PLY**. Select **STL** for 3D printing.

   ![Export panel in the Meshy tab with a folder path and the Format menu open, listing OBJ, PLY, and STL](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/export-panel.png)

5. Optional: Expand **Options**, and change the export options. For what each option does, see [Export options](#export-options).

   ![Export panel with Options expanded, showing the General, Geometry, and Materials checkboxes, with Geometry grayed out for STL](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/export-options.png)

6. Click **Export**.

Blender shows the path of the exported file. To check the file, open it in your slicer or target software.

## Export settings
The folder field and **Format** sit at the top of the **Export** panel.

The folder field accepts a full path or a path that starts with `//`, which means the folder of your Blender file. The default is `//`. Where the file goes depends on these settings:

- If your Blender file is saved, or the folder is a full path, the plugin saves the file in that folder without asking.

- Otherwise, a file browser opens in your home folder, where you choose the location and file name.

The plugin names the file after the Blender file and the active object, such as `MyProject-MyModel.stl`. If the Blender file isn't saved, the name starts with `Untitled`.

**Format** sets the file type: **STL**, **OBJ**, or **PLY**. The default is **STL**. The format also sets which options you can change.

## Export options
Expand **Options** in the **Export** panel to see these settings. They're all off by default.

### General
- **ASCII**: saves an STL or PLY file as text instead of binary. Text files are larger, but you can read and edit them. Not available for OBJ.

- **Scene Scale**: applies the scene's unit scale to the exported file, so other software gets the size you see in Blender. Select it if you changed **Unit Scale** in the scene's unit settings.

### Geometry
Available for OBJ and PLY. STL stores only geometry.

- **UVs**: exports the texture coordinates, which other software needs to show the textures.

- **Normals**: exports the mesh's custom normals if it has them, and calculated normals otherwise. Normals improve shading in other software.

- **Colors**: exports vertex colors, such as the colors of a scanned model.

### Materials
- **Copy Textures**: copies the texture images to the folder of the exported file, so they stay with the model. For OBJ, it also exports the materials. For STL and PLY, the plugin copies the base color texture and gives it the same name as the exported file.

## Supported formats
The following table lists the formats the **Export** panel saves, what each one suits, and what it stores.

| Format | Best for | What it stores |
| --- | --- | --- |
| STL | 3D printing. Slicers such as Cura and PrusaSlicer read it. | Geometry only, with no colors, materials, or textures. Binary or ASCII. |
| OBJ | Sharing models and opening them in other 3D software. | Geometry, UVs, normals, and vertex colors. With **Copy Textures**, also materials and textures. Text only. |
| PLY | Models with vertex colors, such as scans and photogrammetry. | Geometry, UVs, normals, and vertex colors. Binary or ASCII. |

For 3D printing, export a binary STL file, and check the model's dimensions in your slicer.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clicking **Export** does nothing | No object is selected. | Select the objects to export, and then click **Export** again. |
| The OBJ file has no materials | **Copy Textures** is off. For OBJ, the plugin exports materials only with **Copy Textures** selected. | Expand **Options**, select **Copy Textures**, and export again. |

## Next steps
- To take the exported file to your slicer, see [3D printing workflow](/webapp/guides/use-cases/3d-printing).

- To send another model from Meshy to Blender, see [Bridge to Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender).

# Bridge to Cascadeur
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/cascadeur/bridge-to-cascadeur

# Bridge to Cascadeur

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open Cascadeur scene, ready to animate.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Cascadeur** opens the upgrade options.

- You need Cascadeur 2026.2.3 or later. For details, see [Meshy for Cascadeur](/webapp/plugins/cascadeur/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in Cascadeur, follow these steps:

1. Open Cascadeur, and create or open a scene.

2. Click **Scripts > Meshy > Start Cascadeur bridge**.

   ![Cascadeur Scripts menu with Meshy open, showing Start Cascadeur bridge and Stop Cascadeur bridge](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/cascadeur-plugin/screenshot-start-bridge.webp)

3. In the **Event log** tab, check that the bridge is listening on port `5333`.

   ![Cascadeur Event log tab showing that the Meshy Cascadeur bridge started and is listening on port 5333](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/cascadeur-plugin/screenshot-event-log.webp)

Keep Cascadeur open while you send models from Meshy. Start the bridge again each time you open Cascadeur. To stop it, click **Scripts > Meshy > Stop Cascadeur bridge**.

## Send a model
To send a model to Cascadeur, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Rigged character with its skeleton in the Meshy viewer and an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/cascadeur-plugin/screenshot-send-rigged-model.webp)

3. Click **Send to Cascadeur**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a knight model in the Meshy viewer with an arrow pointing to Send to Cascadeur](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/cascadeur-plugin/screenshot-send-to-cascadeur.webp)

Meshy sends the model as a GLB file, and Cascadeur imports it into the open scene. For a rigged or animated character, Meshy sends the mesh with its skeleton and skin, ready to animate in Cascadeur. Meshy animations aren't included. You send a model without a rig, such as a prop, the same way.

![Rigged character from Meshy in the Cascadeur viewport, with its skeleton joints listed in the Outliner](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/cascadeur-plugin/screenshot-imported-rigged-model.webp)

## Other ways to send
You can also send a model from these places:

- In the list of your generations, click **Actions** (the three-dot icon) on the model's card, and then click **DCC Bridge > Send to Cascadeur**.

- In **Community**, open a model that another user shared, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Cascadeur**.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to cascadeur" | Cascadeur isn't open, the bridge isn't running, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | In Cascadeur, click **Scripts > Meshy > Start Cascadeur bridge**, and check the **Event log** for port `5333`. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy. Then send the model again. |
| Meshy shows "Model sent to cascadeur", but the model doesn't appear | Cascadeur downloads and imports the model after Meshy hands it off, and the download or import failed. | Check the **Event log** in Cascadeur for download or import errors. |

## Next steps
- To add a skeleton to a character before you send it, see [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging).

# Meshy plugin for Codex
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/codex/introduction

# Meshy plugin for Codex

Install the Meshy plugin in Codex to generate and texture 3D models from a chat, and save the files in your project.

---

## Overview
The Meshy plugin is in the Plugins Directory that ChatGPT and Codex share. It has two skills:

- **Meshy 3D Generation**: Text to 3D, Image to 3D, and Multi-Image to 3D, AI texturing and retexturing, remeshing to a polygon budget, UV unwrapping, auto-rigging and animation for humanoid characters, and export to GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, or USDZ.
- **Meshy 3D Printing**: printability analysis and repair, single-color and multicolor 3MF, sizing to real-world dimensions, Creative Lab products such as figurines, lamps, keychains, and fridge magnets, and handoff to an installed slicer.

Both skills run the Meshy CLI on your computer. The CLI is the [meshy-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/meshy-cli) package on npm. You sign in once in your browser, and you never paste an API key into the chat.

The plugin saves files in the folder you name, with a rendered preview and the task IDs that Codex needs for follow-up edits. The skills are open source in the [meshy-3d-agent](https://github.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent) repository on GitHub.

---

## Before you begin
- You need Codex, in the ChatGPT desktop app or the Codex CLI. The Meshy plugin doesn't run in ChatGPT in a web browser. On a work or school workspace, an admin might need to allow plugins.

- You need Node.js 22.12 or later, with npm. To check your version, run `node --version`. If Node.js is missing or older, install the current LTS release from the [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org).

- To generate models, you need a paid Meshy plan. Every generation task spends Meshy credits. Local print steps, such as rescaling a model or opening it in a slicer, don't need a sign-in.

---

## Install the plugin
To install the plugin in the ChatGPT desktop app, follow these steps:

1. In the ChatGPT desktop app, switch to **Codex**.

2. Open **Plugins**.

3. Search for Meshy, and then open the Meshy plugin.

4. Click **Install plugin**.

   ![Meshy plugin page in the Codex Plugins Directory with the Install plugin button and three example prompts](https://cdn.meshy.ai/tutorials/how-to-use-meshy-plugin-in-codex/meshy-plugin-chatgpt-plugins-directory.webp)

5. Start a new chat. Codex loads plugins only in chats that you open after the install.

To install the plugin in the Codex CLI, follow these steps:

1. Run `/plugins`.

2. Install **Meshy**.

3. Start a new session.

To confirm the install, type `@` in a new chat and look for Meshy, or ask Codex which Meshy skills are available.

For a step-by-step tutorial, see [How to Use Meshy Plugin in Codex](https://www.meshy.ai/tutorials/how-to-use-meshy-plugin-in-codex).

---

## Sign in
The first time you ask for a model, the plugin checks for the Meshy CLI and a saved Meshy session. If it finds no session, Codex shows a Meshy sign-in link and a one-time code.

To sign in, follow these steps:

1. Open the link.

2. If the page asks for a code, enter the code in **Device code** exactly as Codex shows it, and then click **Continue**.

3. If Meshy asks you to sign in, sign in to your Meshy account.

4. On the **Connect Meshy CLI** page, click **Connect**. The page shows **Meshy CLI authorized**.

   ![Connect Meshy CLI page with the signed-in account, the access the CLI gets, and the Cancel and Connect buttons](/images/ai-agent-plugins/meshy-cli-connect.webp)

5. Return to Codex. Codex continues the request you made.

The code expires after 10 minutes. If it expires, ask Codex for a new one. The Meshy CLI stores the session on your computer and reuses it in later chats. If `MESHY_API_KEY` is set in your environment, the CLI uses that API key instead of the browser session.

In the Codex CLI, the first run might ask for network access. Approve it so the Meshy CLI can reach the Meshy API.

---

## Example prompts
Mention `@Meshy`, or describe the job in your own words. For example:

- *Create a low-poly treasure chest for my game, target 2,000 triangles, add PBR textures, and save it as GLB in ./assets.*
- *Turn this photo into a textured 3D model and keep its proportions.* (attach the image)
- *Rig this textured humanoid character, add a walking animation, and export it as FBX.*
- *Retexture ./assets/chest.glb as weathered bronze and save it beside the original.*
- *Turn this photo into a 75 mm figurine, check its printability, and prepare a multicolor 3MF for a compatible slicer.*

Follow-up requests reuse the previous result, for example *make a 1,500-face LOD*, *now as FBX*, or *scale it to 150 mm*. If you don't name a folder, the plugin saves files in `./meshy_output`.

---

## Credits
Generation, texturing, remeshing, rigging, animation, and repair spend credits from your Meshy account at API rates. Printability analysis is free. For the cost of each task, see [Pricing](/api/pricing).

Before a paid step, Codex estimates its cost, and it asks before it spends more than you approved. To approve each paid step yourself, add *ask me before spending credits* to your request. To check your balance at any time, ask *how many Meshy credits do I have?*

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy doesn't appear after you type `@` | You're in ChatGPT in a web browser, or the chat was open before you installed the plugin. | Use the ChatGPT desktop app or the Codex CLI. Restart Codex, and open a new chat. |
| Codex asks for an API key | The plugin doesn't need one. It signs in through your browser. | Decline, and ask Codex to sign in through the browser instead. Never paste an API key into a chat. |
| `node` or `npm` isn't found | Node.js isn't installed, or Codex can't find it. | Install Node.js 22.12 or later from the [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org), and then restart Codex. |
| The sign-in code expired | A code is valid for 10 minutes. | Ask Codex to start the sign-in again. |
| Codex can't generate because of your plan or credits | Generation needs a paid plan and enough credits. | Check your plan and balance on the [Subscription](https://www.meshy.ai/settings/subscription) page in the Meshy web app. |
| You're signed in to the wrong Meshy account | The Meshy CLI reuses the session that it stored on your computer. | Ask Codex to run `meshy auth logout`, and then sign in again. |

---

## FAQ
### Is the Meshy plugin for Codex free?

The plugin is free to install. Generating 3D models requires a paid Meshy plan and spends Meshy credits at API rates. Printability analysis is free, and local steps, such as rescaling a model or opening it in a slicer, don't need a sign-in.

### Do I need a Meshy API key?

No. The plugin signs in through your browser with a one-time code, and the Meshy CLI stores the session on your computer. Never paste an API key into a chat. If MESHY_API_KEY is already set in your environment, the Meshy CLI uses it instead of the browser session.

### Where are my models saved?

In the folder you name in your request, or in ./meshy_output if you don't name one, together with a preview image and the task IDs. The plugin saves files on your computer, not in the Meshy web app.

### Which file formats can the plugin export?

GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, and USDZ for 3D assets, and single-color or multicolor 3MF for 3D printing.

### Does the plugin work in ChatGPT in a web browser?

No. The Meshy plugin runs in Codex, in the ChatGPT desktop app or the Codex CLI.

### Can I use the same Meshy skills in Claude Code or Cursor?

Yes. The skills are open source in the meshy-3d-agent repository on GitHub, and you can install them in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and other agents. Ask your agent to follow https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/main/INSTALL.md.

---

- To use the same skills in OpenClaw, see [Meshy skill for OpenClaw](/webapp/plugins/openclaw/introduction).

- To call the Meshy API from an AI agent with your own API key, see [AI integration](/api/ai).

# Animated models

Send an animated character from Meshy to Godot with its skeleton and animation, ready to play in your scene.

## Send an animated model
You send an animated model the same way as a static one. Before you start, run the bridge in Godot. For the steps, see [Bridge to Godot](/webapp/plugins/godot/bridge-to-godot).

To send an animated model, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app, open the animated model in the viewer.

2. Select the animation you want to send.

   ![Animated character in the Meshy viewer with Walking, Running, and other animations to choose from](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/16.webp)

3. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

4. Click **Send to Godot**.

Meshy sends the rigged character with the selected animation at 30 frames per second. The plugin saves the files in the model's folder in `res://imported_models`, and adds the character with its skeleton and animation to the open scene.

   ![Animated character in the Godot 3D view with its walking animation track open in the Animation panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/17.webp)

To play the animation, in the **Scene** dock, select the **AnimationPlayer** node, and then click the play button in the **Animation** panel.

   ![Godot Scene dock with the AnimationPlayer node selected under the imported character, and its animation in the Animation panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/18.webp)

# Bridge to Godot
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/godot/bridge-to-godot

# Bridge to Godot

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open Godot scene, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Godot** opens the upgrade options.

- Install and enable the Meshy plugin in your Godot project. For the steps, see [Meshy for Godot](/webapp/plugins/godot/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in Godot, follow these steps:

1. At the top of the Godot editor, click the **Meshy** tab.

2. Click **Run Meshy Bridge**. The status changes to **Bridge: Running**, the button changes to **Stop Meshy Bridge**, and the plugin waits for models from Meshy.

   ![Meshy tab in the Godot editor with Bridge: Stopped and the Run Meshy Bridge and Open Meshy Editor buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/8.webp)

To stop the bridge, click **Stop Meshy Bridge**. The bridge doesn't start on its own, so start it again each time you open the project.

## Send a model
To send a model to Godot, follow these steps:

1. In Godot, open the scene you want to add the model to. If no scene is open, the plugin creates a 3D scene in `res://imported_models` and opens it.

2. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

3. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

4. Click **Send to Godot**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to Godot](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtogodot.webp)

Meshy sends the model as a GLB file. The plugin saves it in its own folder in `res://imported_models`, adds it to the open scene, and selects it.

   ![Godot editor with the imported model in the 3D view, its node in the Scene dock, and imported_models in FileSystem](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/13.webp)

You can send any model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Godot and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/newpanel/doc-moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Godot**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/newpanel/doc-community.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to godot" | Godot isn't open, the bridge isn't running, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | In Godot, click the **Meshy** tab, click **Run Meshy Bridge**, and then send the model again. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy, and then send the model again. |
| The status stays at **Bridge: Stopped** after you click **Run Meshy Bridge** | Another app, or another Godot editor with the bridge running, uses port `5325`. | Close the other app or stop the bridge in the other editor, and then click **Run Meshy Bridge** again. |

## Next steps
- To bring a rigged character and its animation into Godot, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/godot/animated-models).

# Meshy for Godot
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/godot/introduction

# Meshy for Godot

Install the Meshy plugin in the Godot editor so you can send models from the Meshy web app straight into your Godot scenes.

---

## Before you begin
- Download the plugin, a `.zip` file, from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/godot"}>Meshy for Godot integration page</ExternalLink>.

- You need a Meshy account. To send models with the bridge, you need a Pro plan or higher.

## Install the plugin
To install the plugin, follow these steps:

1. Unzip the file you downloaded. It contains a `meshy-godot-plugin` folder.

2. If your project has no `addons` folder, in the Godot **FileSystem** dock, right-click `res://`, and then click **Create New > Folder**.

   ![Godot FileSystem dock with the res:// context menu open and Create New, Folder highlighted](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/2.webp)

3. Enter `addons` as the folder name.

4. Click **OK**.

   ![Godot Create Folder dialog with addons entered as the name and the OK button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/3.webp)
   ![Godot FileSystem dock showing the new addons folder under res://](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/4.webp)

5. Drag the `meshy-godot-plugin` folder into the `addons` folder in the **FileSystem** dock. Keep the folder name as it is, because the plugin loads its files from `res://addons/meshy-godot-plugin`.

   ![Godot FileSystem dock with the meshy-godot-plugin folder and its files inside addons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/5.webp)

6. In the Godot menu bar, click **Project > Project Settings**, and then click the **Plugins** tab.

7. Select the **Enabled** checkbox for **Meshy official plugin**.

   ![Godot Project Settings on the Plugins tab with Meshy official plugin listed and enabled](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/6.webp)

When the plugin is enabled, a **Meshy** tab appears at the top of the editor, next to **AssetLib**. It opens the panel you use to receive models.

   ![Godot editor tabs 2D, 3D, Script, Game, AssetLib, and the Meshy tab added by the plugin](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/7.webp)

## Next steps

# Meshy skills for Hermes Agent
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/hermes-agent/introduction

# Meshy skills for Hermes Agent

Add the Meshy skills to Hermes Agent so your agent can generate 3D models, textures, and animations, and prepare 3D prints, from a chat.

---

## Overview
Meshy has two skills for [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent):

- `meshy-3d-generation`: Text to 3D, Image to 3D, and Multi-Image to 3D, AI texturing and retexturing, remeshing to a polygon budget, UV unwrapping, auto-rigging and animation for humanoid characters, and export to GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, or USDZ.
- `meshy-3d-printing`: printability analysis and repair, single-color and multicolor 3MF, sizing to real-world dimensions, Creative Lab products such as figurines, lamps, keychains, and fridge magnets, and handoff to an installed slicer.

Each skill installs on its own, so you can add only the printing skill if that's all you need. Both skills run the Meshy CLI, which is the [meshy-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/meshy-cli) package on npm. You sign in once in your browser, and you don't need an API key.

The skills are open source in the [meshy-3d-agent](https://github.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent) repository on GitHub.

---

## Before you begin
- You need Hermes Agent.

- You need Node.js 22.12 or later, with npm, on the computer that runs Hermes.

- To generate models, you need a paid Meshy plan. Every generation task spends Meshy credits at API rates. For the cost of each task, see [Pricing](/api/pricing). Printability analysis is free, and local print steps, such as rescaling a model or opening it in a slicer, don't need a sign-in.

---

## Install the skills
To let Hermes do the setup, paste the following text into a chat:

```text
Help me install Meshy CLI and the meshy-3d-agent skills:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/main/INSTALL.md
```

Hermes checks Node.js, installs the Meshy CLI and both skills, and then walks you through the sign-in.

To install the skills yourself, add them from GitHub with Hermes:

```bash
hermes skills install meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/skills/meshy-3d-generation
hermes skills install meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/skills/meshy-3d-printing
```

You can also install both skills with the [skills](https://skills.sh) installer:

```bash
npx -y skills add meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent --skill meshy-3d-generation --skill meshy-3d-printing -g -y -a hermes-agent
```

You don't need a global `npm install -g meshy-cli`. Without it, the skills run the CLI through `npm exec`. A global install only makes startup faster.

If Hermes doesn't use the skills in a conversation that was open while you installed them, start a new session.

---

## Sign in
The first time you ask for a model, Hermes starts the Meshy CLI sign-in and sends you a link and a one-time code.

To sign in, follow these steps:

1. Open the link on any device.

2. If the page asks for a code, enter the code in **Device code** exactly as Hermes shows it, and then click **Continue**.

3. If Meshy asks you to sign in, sign in to your Meshy account.

4. On the **Connect Meshy CLI** page, click **Connect**. The page shows **Meshy CLI authorized**.

   ![Connect Meshy CLI page with the signed-in account, the access the CLI gets, and the Cancel and Connect buttons](/images/ai-agent-plugins/meshy-cli-connect.webp)

5. Return to the chat. Hermes continues the request you made.

The code expires after 10 minutes. If it expires, ask Hermes for a new one. You can approve the sign-in from any browser, so it also works when Hermes runs on a server or over SSH.

The Meshy CLI stores the session in `~/.config/meshy/credentials.json`. Every agent that runs as the same user on that computer shares the session. If `MESHY_API_KEY` is set, the CLI uses that API key instead of the browser session.

---

## Example prompts
Describe the job in your own words. For example:

- *Make a 3D model of a baby husky and save it as GLB in ./assets.*
- *Turn this photo into a textured 3D model and keep its proportions.* (attach the image)
- *Create three low-poly potion bottles for my game, each under 1,500 triangles.*
- *Rig this humanoid character, add a walking animation, and export it as FBX.*
- *Help me 3D print a small dragon figurine, 80 mm tall, as a multicolor 3MF.*

Follow-up requests reuse the previous result, for example *make a 1,500-face LOD*, *now as FBX*, or *scale it to 150 mm*. To approve each paid step yourself, add *ask me before spending credits* to your request.

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hermes doesn't use the Meshy skills | Hermes didn't load the skills in the open conversation, or didn't match your request to them. | Start a new session, or mention Meshy in your request. |
| `node` or `npm` isn't found | Node.js isn't installed, or Hermes can't find it. | Install Node.js 22.12 or later from the [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org), and then restart Hermes. |
| Hermes asks for an API key | The skills don't need one. They sign in through your browser. | Decline, and ask Hermes to sign in through the browser instead. Never paste an API key into a chat. |
| The sign-in code expired | A code is valid for 10 minutes. | Ask Hermes to start the sign-in again. |
| Hermes can't generate because of your plan or credits | Generation needs a paid plan and enough credits. | Check your plan and balance on the [Subscription](https://www.meshy.ai/settings/subscription) page in the Meshy web app. |
| You're signed in to the wrong Meshy account | The Meshy CLI reuses the session that it stored on your computer. | Ask Hermes to run `meshy auth logout`, and then sign in again. |

---

## FAQ
### How do I add Meshy to Hermes Agent?

Ask Hermes to follow https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/main/INSTALL.md, or run hermes skills install meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/skills/meshy-3d-generation and the same command for meshy-3d-printing. You also need Node.js 22.12 or later with npm.

### Do I need a Meshy API key?

No. The skills sign in through your browser with a one-time code, and the Meshy CLI stores the session. If MESHY_API_KEY is already set in your environment, the Meshy CLI uses it instead.

### Can I install only the 3D printing skill?

Yes. meshy-3d-printing installs and works on its own, including the generation steps a print needs.

### Does it work when Hermes runs on a remote server?

Yes. The sign-in shows a link and a code that you can approve from any browser.

### Are these the same skills as the Codex plugin?

Yes. The Codex plugin, Claude Code, Cursor, and Hermes Agent all use meshy-3d-generation and meshy-3d-printing from the open-source meshy-3d-agent repository.

### Is it free?

The skills are free and open source. Generating 3D models requires a paid Meshy plan and spends Meshy credits at API rates. Printability analysis is free.

# Animated models
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/maya/animated-models

# Animated models

Send an animated character from Meshy to Maya with its skeleton and animation, ready to play in your scene.

---

## Send an animated model
You send an animated model the same way as a static one. Before you start, run the bridge in Maya. For the steps, see [Bridge to Maya](/webapp/plugins/maya/bridge-to-maya).

To send an animated model, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app, open the animated model in the viewer.

2. Select the animation you want to send.

   ![Animated ogre in the Meshy viewer with Walking selected among five animations, including Running and Angry Stomp](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/13.png)

3. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

4. Click **Send to Maya**.

Meshy sends the rigged character with the selected animation at 30 frames per second. The plugin imports the character, its skeleton, and its animation into the open scene.

   ![Maya viewport with the imported ogre, its armature in the Outliner, and the Meshy Bridge window showing Bridge ON](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/14.png)

To preview the animation, drag the Time Slider.

   ![Maya viewport with the ogre in mid-stride and an arrow pointing to the Time Slider at frame 18](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/15.png)

## Next steps
- To add more animations to a character before you send it, see [Animation](/webapp/guides/animate).

# Bridge to Maya
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/maya/bridge-to-maya

# Bridge to Maya

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open Maya scene, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Maya** opens the upgrade options.

- Install the Meshy plugin in Maya. For the steps, see [Meshy for Maya](/webapp/plugins/maya/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in Maya, follow these steps:

1. In the Maya menu bar, click **Meshy > Bridge Panel**. The **Meshy Bridge** window opens.

2. Click **Run Bridge**. The button turns green and changes to **Bridge ON**, and the plugin waits for models from Meshy.

   ![Meshy Bridge window in Maya with the gray Run Bridge button, before the bridge starts](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/5.png)

To stop the bridge, click **Bridge ON**.

## Send a model
To send a model to Maya, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to Maya**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to Maya](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtomaya.webp)

Meshy sends the model as an FBX file. The plugin imports it into the open scene, gives its objects names that start with `Meshy_`, and builds a Standard Surface material from its textures.

   ![Maya viewport with the imported woodland model, the model in the Outliner, and the Meshy Bridge window showing Bridge ON](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/10.png)

You can send any model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Maya and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/newpanel/doc-moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Maya**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/maya-plugin/newpanel/doc-community.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to maya" | Maya isn't open, the bridge isn't running, another app uses port `5328`, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | In Maya, click **Meshy > Bridge Panel**, click **Run Bridge**, and then send the model again. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy. If the send still fails, close any other app that uses port `5328`. |
| After you click **Run Bridge**, the button still shows **Run Bridge** | Another app uses port `5328`, such as a second Maya session with the bridge on. | Close the other app or stop its bridge, and then click **Run Bridge** again. |

## Next steps
- To bring a rigged character and its animation into Maya, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/maya/animated-models).
