# Bridge to Omniverse / Isaac Sim
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/omniverse/bridge-to-omniverse

# Bridge to Omniverse / Isaac Sim

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your NVIDIA Omniverse or Isaac Sim stage, with physics and semantic labels applied during import.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to OV/Isaac** opens the upgrade options.

- You need the Meshy web app on Windows. On other operating systems, **Send to OV/Isaac** is unavailable.

- Install the Meshy Bridge extension in Isaac Sim or your Omniverse Kit app. For the steps, see [Meshy for Omniverse / Isaac Sim](/webapp/plugins/omniverse/introduction).

## Start the bridge
The extension runs the bridge while it's enabled, so you don't start anything else.

To get the app ready, follow these steps:

1. Open Isaac Sim or your Omniverse Kit app.

2. Click **Window > Extensions**, and check that **MESHY BRIDGE** is turned on.

   ![Extensions window with MESHY BRIDGE turned on and ENABLED and AUTOLOAD selected](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_enable_bridge.webp)

3. Open or create a USD stage. To create one, click **File > New**.

Keep the app open while you send models from Meshy.

## Send a model
To send a model to Omniverse or Isaac Sim, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on Windows, open a finished model in the viewer.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to OV/Isaac**. Meshy checks that the bridge is running, and then opens the **Sim-Ready Properties** dialog.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to OV/Isaac](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendto_ov_isaac.webp)

4. Optional: Change the Sim-Ready settings. For what each setting does, see [Sim-Ready settings](#configure-sim-ready).

5. In the **Sim-Ready Properties** dialog, click **Send to OV/Isaac**. To cancel without sending, click **Cancel**.

Meshy sends the model as a USDZ file, with the name of the model and your Sim-Ready settings. The extension downloads the file and adds the model to the open stage under `/World`, in a prim named after the model. It also matches the model's up axis and units to the stage.

## Sim-Ready settings
The **Sim-Ready Properties** dialog sets how the model behaves in a physics simulation and how it's labeled. You can send without changing any setting.

![Sim-Ready Properties dialog with Semantic Class set to table, Dynamic and Auto selected, Convex Hull, and friction sliders](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_simready_dialog.webp)

The dialog has the following settings:

- **Semantic Class**: Optional. A class label, such as `chair`, `table`, or `robot`. The extension writes it as a semantic label, and also as a legacy class label for older Isaac Sim versions.
- **Wikidata QCode**: Optional. A Wikidata ID, such as `Q15026`. It starts with `Q`, followed by a number that doesn't start with `0`.
- **Height (m)**: Optional. The model's real-world height in meters. If you leave it empty, the extension scales the model by the units of the file and the stage.
- **Body Type**: **Dynamic** (the default), **Kinematic**, or **Static**.
- **Mass (kg)**: **Auto** (the default), **Mass**, or **Density**. **Auto** sets no mass or density, so the physics engine uses its defaults and the collider shape. **Mass** sets the mass in kilograms. **Density** sets the density in kg/m³, and the label changes to **Density (kg/m³)**. A **Static** body has no mass setting.
- **Collision Approximation**: **Convex Hull** (the default), **Convex Decomposition**, **Mesh Simplification**, **Bounding Cube**, **Bounding Sphere**, or **Triangle Mesh**. For a **Dynamic** body, the list leaves out **Mesh Simplification** and **Triangle Mesh**. SDF collision isn't available.
- **Static Friction**, **Dynamic Friction**, and **Restitution**: Physics material values from `0` to `1` for the model's colliders. The defaults are `0.50`, `0.50`, and `0.00`.

## Check the import
After Meshy shows "Model sent to omniverse", the model appears in the open stage under `/World`.

![Isaac Sim stage with the imported woodland model and its Meshy prim and mesh listed in the Stage panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_result.webp)

The extension adds `UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI` and `UsdPhysics.MeshCollisionAPI` to each mesh in the model. For a dynamic or kinematic body, it also adds `UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI` and `UsdPhysics.MassAPI` to the model's prim.

To test the physics, click **Play** in Isaac Sim. A dynamic body moves with the simulation, and a static body stays in place. A kinematic body moves only by animation or script, and other bodies still collide with it.

## Send an animated model
You send an animated model the same way as a static one. Meshy sends the rigged character with the selected animation. Smart Rig models don't have **DCC Bridge**, so you can't send them.

![Animated Roman soldier imported into Isaac Sim, with its armature and mesh listed in the Stage panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_animated_model.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to omniverse" before the **Sim-Ready Properties** dialog opens | Isaac Sim or your Kit app isn't open, or the extension is off. | Open the app, and turn on **MESHY BRIDGE** in **Window > Extensions**. Then send the model again. |
| The dialog opens, but the send fails, and `http://127.0.0.1:5331/status` in your browser doesn't show `"dcc": "omniverse"` | Another app uses port `5331`, so the extension can't start its bridge. | Close the other app, and then turn **MESHY BRIDGE** off and on again in **Window > Extensions**. Check that the status page shows `"dcc": "omniverse"`. |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to omniverse" after you click **Send to OV/Isaac** in the dialog, and the status page shows `"dcc": "omniverse"` | No USD stage is open. The app's **Console** shows `no active USD stage`. | Open or create a stage with **File > New**, and then send the model again. |
| **Send to OV/Isaac** in the dialog is unavailable | **Wikidata QCode**, **Height (m)**, or the mass or density value isn't valid. | Enter a QCode in the format `Q15026`, and a height, mass, or density greater than `0`. |
| **Send to OV/Isaac** in the **DCC Bridge** menu is unavailable | You use the Meshy web app on macOS or Linux. | Use the Meshy web app on Windows. |

## Next steps
- To add an animation to a character before you send it, see [Animation](/webapp/guides/animate).

# Meshy for Omniverse / Isaac Sim
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/omniverse/introduction

# Meshy for Omniverse / Isaac Sim

Install the Meshy Bridge extension in NVIDIA Omniverse or Isaac Sim so you can send models from the Meshy web app straight into your open USD stage.

---

## Before you begin
- Download the extension, a `.zip` file, from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/omniverse"}>Meshy for Omniverse integration page</ExternalLink>.

- You need Isaac Sim or another Omniverse Kit app, running on the same computer as your browser.

- You need the Meshy web app on Windows. **Send to OV/Isaac** isn't available on other operating systems.

- You need a Meshy account. To send models with the bridge, you need a Pro plan or higher.

Meshy tested the extension with Isaac Sim 6.0.0.

![Isaac Sim with an imported Meshy character on the stage and the Meshy Bridge details in the Extensions tab](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_download.webp)

## Install the extension
To install the extension, follow these steps:

1. In Isaac Sim or your Omniverse Kit app, click **Window > Extensions**.

   ![Isaac Sim Window menu with Window and Extensions outlined in red](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_open_extensions.webp)

2. In the **Extensions** window, click the menu icon (☰), and then click **Import Extension**.

   ![Extensions window with the menu icon open and Import Extension outlined in red under Options](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_extension_menu.webp)

3. In the **Choose Extension Zip Archive** dialog, select the `.zip` file you downloaded, and then click **Import**.

   ![Choose Extension Zip Archive dialog with the ai.meshy.bridge-0.1.0.zip file selected and the Import button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_extension_zip.webp)

## Enable the extension
To enable the extension, follow these steps:

1. In the **Extensions** window, search for `Meshy Bridge`.

2. Select **MESHY BRIDGE**, and turn on its toggle.

3. Optional: Select **AUTOLOAD** so the extension starts each time you open the app.

![Extensions window with MESHY BRIDGE turned on, ENABLED and AUTOLOAD selected, and the extension overview](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_enable_bridge.webp)

When the extension is on, it listens for models from Meshy on `127.0.0.1:5331`. If the app is closed or the extension is off, Meshy can't connect to Omniverse.

## Sim-Ready settings
Each time you send a model to Omniverse or Isaac Sim, Meshy opens the **Sim-Ready Properties** dialog. In it, you set how the model behaves in a physics simulation: body type, mass, collision, and friction. You can also set the model's real-world height, a semantic class, and an optional Wikidata QCode. For each setting, see [Bridge to Omniverse / Isaac Sim](/webapp/plugins/omniverse/bridge-to-omniverse#configure-sim-ready).

# Meshy skill for OpenClaw
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/openclaw/introduction

# Meshy skill for OpenClaw

Add the Meshy skill to OpenClaw so your agent can generate 3D models, textures, and animations, and prepare 3D prints, from a chat.

---

## Overview
The Meshy skill is on ClawHub as [Meshy 3D Agent](https://clawhub.ai/arlieeee/skills/meshy-3d-agent). This one skill covers both workflows:

- **3D generation**: Text to 3D, Image to 3D, and Multi-Image to 3D, AI texturing and retexturing, remeshing to a polygon budget, UV unwrapping, auto-rigging and animation for humanoid characters, and export to GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, or USDZ.
- **3D printing**: printability analysis and repair, single-color and multicolor 3MF, sizing to real-world dimensions, Creative Lab products such as figurines, lamps, keychains, and fridge magnets, and handoff to an installed slicer such as Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, or Creality Print.

The skill runs the Meshy CLI, which is the [meshy-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/meshy-cli) package on npm. You sign in once in your browser, and you don't need an API key.

---

## Before you begin
- You need [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai).

- You need Node.js 22.12 or later, with npm, on the computer that runs OpenClaw. OpenClaw makes the skill available when `meshy` or `npm` is on `PATH`.

- To generate models, you need a paid Meshy plan. Every generation task spends Meshy credits at API rates. For the cost of each task, see [Pricing](/api/pricing). Printability analysis is free, and local print steps, such as rescaling a model or opening it in a slicer, don't need a sign-in.

---

## Install the skill
To install the skill from ClawHub, run the following command:

```bash
openclaw skills install @arlieeee/meshy-3d-agent
```

If the Meshy CLI isn't installed, OpenClaw's Skills page can offer to install it from npm. You don't need a global install. Without one, the skill runs the CLI through `npm exec`, and a global install only makes startup faster.

To let OpenClaw do the whole setup instead, paste the following text into a chat:

```text
Help me install Meshy CLI and the meshy-3d-agent skills:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/main/INSTALL.md
```

An open session picks up the skill on its next turn. If you installed Node.js or the Meshy CLI while a session was open, start a new session so OpenClaw finds them.

---

## Sign in
The first time you ask for a model, OpenClaw starts the Meshy CLI sign-in and sends you a link and a one-time code.

To sign in, follow these steps:

1. Open the link on any device.

2. If the page asks for a code, enter the code in **Device code** exactly as OpenClaw shows it, and then click **Continue**.

3. If Meshy asks you to sign in, sign in to your Meshy account.

4. On the **Connect Meshy CLI** page, click **Connect**. The page shows **Meshy CLI authorized**.

   ![Connect Meshy CLI page with the signed-in account, the access the CLI gets, and the Cancel and Connect buttons](/images/ai-agent-plugins/meshy-cli-connect.webp)

5. Return to the chat. OpenClaw continues the request you made.

The code expires after 10 minutes. If it expires, ask OpenClaw for a new one. You can approve the sign-in from any browser, so it also works when OpenClaw runs on a server or in a container.

You don't need `MESHY_API_KEY`. If it's set, the CLI uses that API key instead of the browser session.

---

## Example prompts
Describe the job in your own words. For example:

- *Make a 3D model of a baby husky and save it as GLB in ./assets.*
- *Turn this photo into a textured 3D model and keep its proportions.* (attach the image)
- *Rig this humanoid character, add a running animation, and export it as FBX.*
- *Help me 3D print a small dragon figurine, 80 mm tall, and open it in Bambu Studio.*
- *Turn this logo into a keychain I can 3D print.*

Follow-up requests reuse the previous result, for example *make a 1,500-face LOD*, *now as FBX*, or *scale it to 150 mm*. To approve each paid step yourself, add *ask me before spending credits* to your request.

---

## Security and data
The following list summarizes how the skill handles commands, credentials, network access, and files:

- **What it runs**: Only the Meshy CLI, as `meshy` or as the pinned package through `npm exec`. The skill is Markdown only, with no Python, `curl`, or bundled scripts.
- **Credentials**: The CLI stores and refreshes the session in `~/.config/meshy/credentials.json` with mode `0600`. The skill never reads, prints, or copies a token, device code, or key, and never asks for one in chat.
- **Network**: The CLI sends prompts, images, and task requests to the Meshy API, normally `api.meshy.ai`. npm contacts its registry when it installs the CLI or runs it as a temporary package.
- **Files**: Each job writes only inside one folder, the one you named or `./meshy_output`. The CLI refuses paths outside that folder, and doesn't overwrite existing files unless you ask.

For the full security manifest, see [meshy-openclaw](https://github.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent/tree/main/skills/meshy-openclaw) on GitHub.

---

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The skill isn't available in OpenClaw | Neither `meshy` nor `npm` is on `PATH`. | Install Node.js 22.12 or later with npm, and then start a new session. |
| OpenClaw asks for an API key | The skill doesn't need one. It signs in through your browser. | Decline, and ask OpenClaw to sign in through the browser instead. Never paste an API key into a chat. |
| The sign-in code expired | A code is valid for 10 minutes. | Ask OpenClaw to start the sign-in again. |
| OpenClaw can't generate because of your plan or credits | Generation needs a paid plan and enough credits. | Check your plan and balance on the [Subscription](https://www.meshy.ai/settings/subscription) page in the Meshy web app. |
| You're signed in to the wrong Meshy account | The Meshy CLI reuses the session that it stored on your computer. | Ask OpenClaw to run `meshy auth logout`, and then sign in again. |

---

## FAQ
### What is the Meshy skill for OpenClaw?

Meshy 3D Agent is the Meshy skill on ClawHub. It lets an OpenClaw agent generate 3D models, textures, rigging, and animation, and prepare models for 3D printing, by running the Meshy CLI.

### How do I install the Meshy skill in OpenClaw?

Run openclaw skills install @arlieeee/meshy-3d-agent. You also need Node.js 22.12 or later with npm. OpenClaw's Skills page can offer to install the Meshy CLI from npm.

### Do I need a Meshy API key?

No. The skill signs in through your browser with a one-time code, and the Meshy CLI stores the session. You don't need MESHY_API_KEY, but if it's set, the Meshy CLI uses it instead.

### Does the skill work when OpenClaw runs on a server?

Yes. The sign-in shows a link and a code that you can approve from any browser, so OpenClaw can run on a remote computer or in a container.

### Is the Meshy skill free?

The skill is free to install. Generating 3D models requires a paid Meshy plan and spends Meshy credits at API rates. Printability analysis is free.

### I used the older Python-based Meshy OpenClaw skill. Do my tasks still work?

Yes. The skill moved to the Meshy CLI in version 0.6.0, and you can still use task IDs from the old skill with the CLI.

---

- To use the same workflows in Codex, see [Meshy plugin for Codex](/webapp/plugins/codex/introduction).

- To use the same workflows in Hermes Agent, see [Meshy skills for Hermes Agent](/webapp/plugins/hermes-agent/introduction).

- To call the Meshy API from an AI agent with your own API key, see [AI integration](/api/ai).

# Bridge to Roblox
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/roblox/bridge-to-roblox

# Bridge to Roblox

Send a model from the Meshy web app to your Roblox inventory, with no app to install, and use it in Roblox Studio.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Roblox** opens the upgrade options.

- You need a global Roblox account. For the requirements, see [Meshy for Roblox](/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction).

- The model must be 20 MB or smaller, and it can't be rigged or animated. To keep a model under the limit, finish it in this order: generate, remesh, and then texture. Remeshing reduces the face count and the file size.

## Connect your Roblox account
You connect your Roblox account the first time you send a model. To connect it, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to Roblox**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to Roblox](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtoroblox.webp)

4. In the **Send to Roblox, no app needed** dialog, click **Continue**. Meshy shows this dialog only the first time you send from a browser.

   ![Send to Roblox, no app needed dialog explaining the one-time account connection, with the Continue button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v2.0/doc_roblox_intro.webp)

5. In the **Connect to Roblox** dialog, click **Connect**. A Roblox authorization popup opens.

   ![Connect to Roblox dialog in the Meshy web app with the Cancel and Connect buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v2.0/doc_roblox_connect.webp)

6. In the popup, sign in to Roblox if it asks you to, and then click **Continue**.

7. Under **Accounts**, click **Select** next to your Roblox account, and then click **Continue**.

8. Review the permissions, and then click **Confirm and Give Access**.

The following images show the pages of the Roblox authorization popup in order.

![Roblox authorization popup showing the signed-in Roblox account with the Continue and Change Account buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_oauth_login.webp)
<p style={{textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "#666", margin: "4px 0 0"}}>1. Sign in and continue</p>
![Roblox page titled Meshy for Roblox is Requesting Access, listing the Write Assets and Read Assets permissions](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_oauth_permissions.webp)
<p style={{textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "#666", margin: "4px 0 0"}}>2. View the requested permissions</p>
![Roblox Accounts list with arrows pointing to the Select button for the account and to the Continue button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_oauth_account.webp)
<p style={{textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "#666", margin: "4px 0 0"}}>3. Select the account and continue</p>

![Roblox review page listing the permissions Meshy gets and the Roblox account they apply to](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_oauth_review.webp)
<p style={{textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "#666", margin: "4px 0 0"}}>4. Review the permissions</p>
![End of the Roblox review page with the Back and Confirm and Give Access buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_oauth_confirm.webp)
<p style={{textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "#666", margin: "4px 0 0"}}>5. Confirm and give access</p>

After you confirm, the popup closes, and Meshy continues the upload. You don't need to click **Send to Roblox** again.

You connect only once. Meshy keeps your Roblox account connected for later uploads.

## Switch to another Roblox account
To send models to a different Roblox account, follow these steps:

1. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge**.

2. Hover over **Send to Roblox**, and then click **Switch Account** (the user icon). The icon appears only while a Roblox account is connected.

3. In the **Roblox Account Connected** dialog, click **Switch Account**. Meshy disconnects the current account.

4. Click **Connect**, and then give Meshy access to the other account in the Roblox popup. If the popup shows your previous account, click **Change Account** first.

Switching disconnects your previous Roblox account from Meshy. Assets you already uploaded stay in that account.

## Send a model
After you connect your Roblox account, you send models without authorizing again. To send a model, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app, open the model in the viewer.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Roblox**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu with the pointer on Send to Roblox, showing its Download Plugin and Guide icons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_bridge_connected.webp)

Meshy uploads the model to your Roblox inventory as a private GLB asset. The asset name starts with `Meshy_`.

You can send any static model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a warrior model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Roblox and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Roblox**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc-community.webp)

## Open the uploaded model
When the upload finishes, Meshy shows the **Uploaded to Roblox** dialog with the asset ID.

   ![Uploaded to Roblox dialog with the asset ID and the Copy Asset ID, Open in Creator Hub, and Open in Studio buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v2.0/doc_roblox_success.webp)

In the dialog, you can click the following:

- **Open in Creator Hub**: Opens the asset in your Roblox Creator Hub, where you can manage it.

  ![Roblox Creator Hub Configure page for the uploaded Meshy asset, with its name, description, and an untextured preview](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_creatorhub.webp)

- **Open in Studio**: Opens Roblox Studio with a default scene that contains only the model you uploaded. Use this temporary scene to view the asset.

  ![Roblox Studio with the uploaded Meshy model in the scene, selected in the Explorer, and shown in the Toolbox](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_studio_model.webp)

- **Copy Asset ID**: Copies the Roblox asset ID to your clipboard.

> **Note:** The Creator Hub web preview might not show the textures of a larger model correctly. This affects only the Roblox web viewer. The textures appear as expected when you import the model into Roblox Studio.

Roblox reviews every new asset. Until the review finishes, the asset might not appear in Creator Hub or Studio. The review usually takes a few minutes.

## Find your models in Roblox Studio
To find every model you sent to Roblox, follow these steps:

1. In Roblox Studio, open the **Toolbox**.

2. Click the **Inventory** tab.

3. In the drop-down list, select **My Packages**.

   ![Roblox Studio Toolbox with My Packages selected, showing an uploaded Meshy model](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_toolbox_packages.webp)

## Use the legacy desktop app
You don't need the Meshy Roblox Bridge desktop app to send models. If you already use it, it keeps working. If you choose **Keep using desktop app**, Meshy sends your models through the app while it's running and connected to your Roblox account. When an upload finishes, the app window comes to the front, with links to open the asset.

The first time you click **Send to Roblox** with the desktop app set up, Meshy asks whether to keep using it. Click **Keep using desktop app** or **Try the new way**. Meshy keeps your choice for later sends.

To stop using the app later, quit it, and then click **Send to Roblox**. In the message that Meshy shows, click **Use without the app**, and then connect your Roblox account in the browser. If the app is running but isn't connected to Roblox, the **Connect to Roblox** dialog also shows **Use without the app**.

To download the app, go to the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/roblox"}>Meshy for Roblox integration page</ExternalLink>, and expand **Legacy desktop app**. To open the app on macOS for the first time, see [Allow the legacy app on macOS](/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction#macos-gatekeeper).

### View the upload history
The desktop app keeps a record of the models you sent through it. To see the record, expand **Upload History** in the app window.

   ![Meshy Roblox Bridge window with an Upload History entry and its Creator Hub, Open in Studio, and Copy Asset ID links](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_bridge_history.webp)

In the upload history, you can do the following:

- To open or copy an asset, click **Creator Hub**, **Open in Studio**, or **Copy Asset ID** under the model.

- To delete one record, click the X icon next to it.

- To delete all records, click **Clear All**.

> **Note:** The desktop app stores the upload history on your computer. Clearing it doesn't affect the assets in your Roblox account. Models you send without the desktop app don't appear in this history, so find them in Creator Hub or the Studio Toolbox.

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Roblox authorization popup doesn't open, and Meshy shows "Roblox authorization failed" | Your browser blocked the popup. | Allow popups for `meshy.ai` in your browser settings, and then click **Connect** again. |
| The popup closed, but your Roblox account isn't connected | The popup closed before you confirmed access on Roblox. | In the **Connect to Roblox** dialog, click **Connect**, and finish the authorization on roblox.com. |
| Meshy asks you to connect your Roblox account again | The Roblox authorization expired, or you removed Meshy's access in Roblox. | Click **Connect**, and authorize your account again. Meshy then continues the upload. |
| Meshy shows "Model exceeds Roblox upload size limit (20MB)" | Roblox accepts models up to 20 MB. | Use [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) to reduce the model's face count, and then send the remeshed model. |
| **Send to Roblox** is unavailable for a rigged or animated model | Meshy sends only static models to Roblox. | Send the static model instead, or download the animated model and import it by hand. |
| The asset doesn't appear in Creator Hub or Studio | Roblox is still reviewing the asset. | Wait a few minutes, and then refresh. To check the asset later, use **Copy Asset ID**. |
| Meshy shows "Upload timed out" and asks you to check your Roblox inventory | Roblox took longer than 3 minutes to process the upload, and Meshy stopped waiting. | Check your inventory in Creator Hub. The upload might have finished after the timeout. |
| Meshy shows "Upload failed" or an error message from Roblox | Roblox rejected the upload, or the connection failed during the upload. | Send the model again. If it keeps failing, disconnect and reconnect your Roblox account. For the steps, see [Switch to another Roblox account](#switch-account). |
| Meshy asks you to start the Meshy Roblox Bridge app | You chose to keep using the desktop app, and the app isn't running. | Open the desktop app, and then send the model again. To send without the app, click **Use without the app** in the message. |

## Next steps
- To reduce a model's size before you send it, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

- To review what you need to use Meshy with Roblox, see [Meshy for Roblox](/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction).

# Meshy for Roblox
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction

# Meshy for Roblox

Send models from the Meshy web app to your Roblox inventory and use them in Roblox Studio, with no app to install.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Meshy Pro plan or higher.

- You need a global Roblox account. To create one, go to [Roblox](https://www.roblox.com).

- Meshy doesn't work with Roblox accounts from mainland China (`roblox.qq.com` or `roblox.cn`), which a regional partner runs with a separate account system. From mainland China, you need a network proxy or VPN to reach `roblox.com`, and a global Roblox account. **Send to Roblox** isn't available on meshy.cn.

There's nothing to install. You connect your Roblox account in the browser and send models from the Meshy web app. Meshy uploads each model as a GLB asset to your Creator Hub inventory. For the steps, see [Bridge to Roblox](/webapp/plugins/roblox/bridge-to-roblox).

If you already use the Meshy Roblox Bridge desktop app, it keeps working, but you don't need it. For details, see [Use the legacy desktop app](/webapp/plugins/roblox/bridge-to-roblox#legacy-desktop-bridge).

## Allow the legacy app on macOS
This section applies only to the legacy desktop app. If you send models from the Meshy web app without the app, skip it.

Meshy distributes the Meshy Roblox Bridge desktop app outside the Mac App Store, and Apple might not have notarized it. As a result, macOS Gatekeeper can block the app from opening, with a warning that Apple can't verify the app. The wording of the warning depends on your macOS version.

   ![macOS warning that MeshyRobloxBridge wasn't opened because Apple could not verify it, with an arrow pointing to Done](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_warning.webp)

To allow the app in System Settings, which is the recommended way, follow these steps:

1. In the warning dialog, click **Done**.

2. Go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security**.

3. In the **Security** section, find the message that says MeshyRobloxBridge was blocked, and click **Open Anyway**.

   ![macOS Privacy and Security settings with a message that MeshyRobloxBridge was blocked and arrows pointing to Open Anyway](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_settings.webp)

4. In the confirmation dialog, click **Open Anyway**.

   ![macOS dialog asking whether to open MeshyRobloxBridge, with an arrow pointing to Open Anyway](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_open.webp)

5. Enter an administrator user name and password, and then click **OK**.

   ![macOS Privacy and Security prompt asking for an administrator user name and password to allow the app](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_password.webp)

The app opens, and its window shows **Server** as **Running**.

   ![Meshy Roblox Bridge window with Server Running, Roblox Account Not Connected, and a collapsed Upload History](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_bridge_running.webp)

To allow the app in Terminal instead, open **Terminal** and run the following command:

```bash
xattr -cr /path/to/MeshyRobloxBridge.app
```

Replace `/path/to/MeshyRobloxBridge.app` with the path to the app, such as `~/Downloads/MeshyRobloxBridge.app`. After the command runs, double-click the app to open it.

> **Note:** You need to allow the app only one time. After you allow it, macOS doesn't show the Gatekeeper warning for it again.

## Next steps
- To connect your Roblox account and send your first model, see [Bridge to Roblox](/webapp/plugins/roblox/bridge-to-roblox).

# Bridge to Unity
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/unity/bridge-to-unity

# Bridge to Unity

Send a model from the Meshy web app straight into your open Unity scene, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to Unity** opens the upgrade options.

- Install the Meshy plugin in your Unity project. For the steps, see [Meshy for Unity](/webapp/plugins/unity/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in Unity, follow these steps:

1. In the Unity menu bar, click **Meshy > Bridge**. The **Meshy Bridge** window opens, and the bridge starts. The button shows **Bridge ON** while the plugin waits for models from Meshy.

2. If the button shows **Run Bridge**, click it.

3. Optional: Clear **Stand on Ground** if you don't want the plugin to place each imported model on the Y=0 plane. It's selected by default.

   ![Meshy Bridge window in Unity with the Bridge ON button and the Stand on Ground checkbox selected](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_unity_panel.webp)

Keep the **Meshy Bridge** window open while you send models. To stop the bridge, click **Bridge ON**, or close the window.

## Send a model
To send a model to Unity, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to Unity**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy web app with an arrow pointing to Send to Unity](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_sendtounity.webp)

Meshy sends the model as an FBX file. The plugin saves it in a new folder in `Assets/MeshyImports`, named after the model, and adds it to the open scene.

   ![Unity editor with the imported model in the Scene view and Meshy_Model selected in the Hierarchy](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_unity_result.webp)

With **Stand on Ground** selected, the model rests on the Y=0 plane.

   ![Imported character standing on the ground plane in the Unity Scene view, with Stand on Ground selected in the Meshy Bridge window](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_unity_stand.webp)

You can send any model in your generations, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a dragon model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to Unity and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc-moredcc.webp)

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to Unity**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc-community.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to unity" | Unity isn't open, the **Meshy Bridge** window is closed or shows **Run Bridge**, another app uses port `5326`, or your browser blocks access to your local network. | In Unity, click **Meshy > Bridge**. If the button shows **Run Bridge**, click it. Then send the model again. If your browser asks for local network access, allow it for Meshy. If the send still fails, close any other app that uses port `5326`. |

## Next steps
- To bring a rigged character and its animation into Unity, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/unity/animated-models).

# Meshy for Unreal
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/unreal/introduction

# Meshy for Unreal

Install the Meshy plugin in Unreal Engine so you can send models from the Meshy web app straight into the level you have open in Unreal Editor.

---

## Before you begin
- Download the plugin from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/unreal-engine"}>Meshy for Unreal Engine integration page</ExternalLink>. The plugin has a separate build for each engine version, as follows.

  - On Windows, download the build for your engine version: UE 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, or 5.7. Each build works only with the engine version it's made for.

  - On macOS, or for an engine version without its own build, download the source package. It contains the plugin source code, which you compile yourself. On macOS, the plugin needs UE 5.5 or later.

- You need a Meshy account. To send models with the bridge, you need a Pro plan or higher.

## Install the plugin
You can install the plugin in the engine, for all your projects, or in a single project.

To install the plugin, follow these steps:

1. Unzip the file you downloaded into one of the following folders:

   - For all projects: the engine's `Engine/Plugins` folder, such as `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.x\Engine\Plugins` on Windows or `/Users/Shared/Epic Games/UE_5.x/Engine/Plugins` on macOS.

   - For one project: the `Plugins` folder in your project folder. If the folder doesn't exist, create it.

   The file contains a `meshy` folder, so the plugin ends up in `Plugins/meshy`.

2. Open your project in Unreal Editor.

3. Click **Edit > Plugins**, and make sure **meshy** is enabled.

4. If you enabled the plugin in the preceding step, restart the editor.

When the plugin loads, the **Window** menu shows a **Meshy Bridge** item. You use it to start and stop the bridge that receives models from Meshy.

   ![Unreal Editor Window menu open, with an arrow pointing to the Meshy Bridge item and its empty checkbox](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unreal-plugin/2.png)

## Next steps
- To send your first model from Meshy to Unreal, see [Bridge to Unreal Engine](/webapp/plugins/unreal/bridge-to-unreal).

- To import a rigged character with its animation, see [Animated models](/webapp/plugins/unreal/animated-models).

# Troubleshooting
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/unreal/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

Fix problems with models that the Meshy plugin imports into Unreal Engine.

---

## Textures appear blurry

After the plugin imports a model, its textures look blurry in the level. They turn sharp only after you click the model's asset in the **Content Browser**.

This happens because Unreal streams textures in progressively, so it shows them at a lower resolution first. To make Unreal load the textures in use at full resolution, follow these steps:

1. In the Unreal Editor status bar, click the console box next to **Cmd**.

2. Enter `r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures 1`, and then press Enter.

   ![Unreal Editor status bar with r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures 1 entered in the console box next to Cmd](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unreal-plugin/14.png)

The textures in the level turn sharp.

## Next steps
- To fix a model that doesn't arrive in Unreal, see [Bridge to Unreal Engine](/webapp/plugins/unreal/bridge-to-unreal#troubleshooting).

# Bridge to ZBrush
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/zbrush/bridge-to-zbrush

# Bridge to ZBrush

Send a model from the Meshy web app to ZBrush and import it as a tool to sculpt, without downloading and importing the file by hand.

---

## Before you begin
- You need a Pro plan or higher. On the Free and Starter plans, clicking **Send to ZBrush** opens the upgrade options.

- Install the Meshy plugin in ZBrush 2025.1 or later. For the steps, see [Meshy for ZBrush](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/introduction).

## Start the bridge
To start the bridge in ZBrush, follow these steps:

1. In ZBrush, click **Zplugin > Meshy Bridge > Load Meshy Bridge**.

   ![ZBrush Zplugin menu with Meshy Bridge expanded and its Load Meshy Bridge button highlighted](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/load-meshy-bridge.webp)

2. In the **Meshy** menu, check that **Run Bridge** is orange. Orange means the bridge is on and waiting for models from Meshy.

   ![Meshy menu in ZBrush with Run Bridge highlighted orange, followed by Import Pending, Wait for Model, and other buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/run-bridge-orange.webp)

The plugin starts the bridge when it loads. ZBrush's Python can't run a server, so the bridge runs as a separate background process, and it stops when you quit ZBrush. To turn the bridge off or on, click **Run Bridge**.

## Send a model
To send a model to ZBrush, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app on a computer, open the model in the viewer. **DCC Bridge** isn't available on mobile.

2. In the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon).

   ![Meshy web app viewer with an arrow pointing to the DCC Bridge icon in the toolbar](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/send-to-dcc.webp)

3. Click **Send to ZBrush**.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy viewer with an arrow pointing to Send to ZBrush](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/send-to-zbrush.webp)

Meshy sends the model as an OBJ file. The plugin downloads it in the background and keeps it as a pending model until you import it.

You can't send an animated model to ZBrush. For an animated model, **Send to ZBrush** is unavailable. Download the model and import it by hand instead.

## Import pending models
Because of a ZBrush plugin limitation, the plugin doesn't import a model as soon as it arrives. You import it yourself.

To import the models that Meshy sent, follow these steps:

1. In the **Meshy** menu, click **Import Pending**.

   ![Meshy menu in ZBrush with the Import Pending button outlined in red](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/import-pending.webp)

   The plugin imports each pending model as a new tool in the **Tool** palette. The model is white, with **BasicMaterial** applied. The plugin also saves the tool in the `ZTools/Meshy` folder of your ZBrush installation, or in `Lightbox/Tools/Meshy` if there's no `ZTools` folder, so you can reuse it.

   ![ZBrush canvas with the imported woodland model in white and its tool thumbnail outlined in the Tool palette](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/imported-tool.webp)

2. Optional: To show the model's base color, click **Tool > Texture Map**, and then select the texture whose name matches your model. The plugin already loaded the texture and flipped it vertically for ZBrush, so you don't need to set it up.

   ![ZBrush Texture Map panel open with the model's texture selected in Quick Pick and the textured model on the canvas](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/texture-map.webp)

To have the plugin import the next model for you, click **Wait for Model** before you send it. For the next 90 seconds, ZBrush waits for a model from Meshy and imports it when it arrives. ZBrush doesn't respond to other actions until a model arrives or the 90 seconds end.

   ![ZBrush menu bar with a message that Meshy is waiting for your send, with 56 seconds left](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/wait-for-model.webp)

## Other ways to send
You can send any model in your generations that isn't animated, whichever tool made it, except a Smart Rig result or an Ultra 4K model.

   ![DCC Bridge menu open on a textured golem model in the Meshy viewer, listing Send to ZBrush and other targets](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/more-entries.webp)

From the list of your generations, click **Actions** (the three-dot icon) on a model's card, and then click **DCC Bridge > Send to ZBrush**.

You can also send a model that another user shared in **Community**. Open the model, click **DCC Bridge**, and then click **Send to ZBrush**.

   ![Meshy Community page with a grid of models shared by other users](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/community.webp)

## Troubleshooting
The following table lists common problems, their causes, and how to fix them.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meshy shows "Failed to send model to zbrush" | ZBrush isn't open, the plugin isn't loaded, or the bridge is off. | In ZBrush, click **Zplugin > Meshy Bridge > Load Meshy Bridge**, check that **Run Bridge** is orange, and then send the model again. |
| **Run Bridge** is orange, but Meshy shows "Failed to send model to zbrush" | Another app uses port `5332`. The plugin can't tell that app from its own bridge, so **Run Bridge** still turns orange. | Close the other app, and then click **Run Bridge** twice to turn the bridge off and on. |
| **Import Pending** shows "No pending models." | The send hasn't finished, or it failed. | Wait until Meshy shows "Model sent to zbrush", and then click **Import Pending** again. To see whether the bridge is running and how many models are waiting, click **Check Status**. |

## Next steps
- To lower the face count of a model before you send it, see [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh).

# Meshy for ZBrush
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/zbrush/introduction

# Meshy for ZBrush

Install the Meshy plugin in ZBrush so you can send models from the Meshy web app to ZBrush and use them as a starting point for your sculpt.

---

## Before you begin
- You need ZBrush 2025.1 or later. The plugin uses the ZBrush Python API, which earlier versions don't have.

- You need macOS or Windows. Each download includes its own Python runtime, so you don't need to install Python.

- You need a Meshy account. To send models with the bridge, you need a Pro plan or higher.

## Install the plugin
To install the plugin, follow these steps:

1. In the Meshy web app, open a model that isn't animated, and then in the viewer toolbar, click **DCC Bridge** (the plug icon). For an animated model, **Send to ZBrush** shows no download icon.

2. Hold the pointer over **Send to ZBrush**, and then click **Download Plugin** (the download icon). The Meshy for ZBrush integration page opens.

   ![DCC Bridge menu in the Meshy viewer with arrows pointing to the DCC Bridge icon and the Send to ZBrush download icon](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/dcc-bridge-download.webp)

3. Under **Choose your platform**, select **macOS** or **Windows**, and then click **Download Plugin**.

   ![Meshy for ZBrush integration page with macOS selected under Choose your platform and the Download Plugin button](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/plugin-detail-download.webp)

4. Open the download. On macOS, open the `.dmg` file. On Windows, extract the `.zip` file.

5. Copy `MeshyBridge.zsc` and the `MeshyBridgeData` folder into the `ZData/ZPlugs64` folder of your ZBrush installation. For example:

   - macOS: `/Applications/Maxon ZBrush 2026/ZData/ZPlugs64`
   - Windows: `C:\Program Files\Maxon ZBrush 2026\ZData\ZPlugs64`

   ![macOS Finder window with MeshyBridgeData and MeshyBridge.zsc inside the ZPlugs64 folder of Maxon ZBrush 2026](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/zplugs64.webp)

6. On macOS only, clear the quarantine flag on the `MeshyBridgeData` folder, so ZBrush can start the Python runtime that comes with the plugin. macOS quarantines the runtime because the build isn't notarized. In Terminal, run the following command once:

   ```bash
   xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Maxon ZBrush 2026/ZData/ZPlugs64/MeshyBridgeData"
   ```

   If you skip this step, macOS blocks the Python runtime and shows an error like the following:

   ![macOS dialog saying Failed to open python3.11 because Apple can't verify it, with Done and Move to Trash buttons](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/macos-error.webp)

7. Restart ZBrush.

8. Click **Zplugin > Meshy Bridge > Load Meshy Bridge**.

   ![ZBrush Zplugin menu with Meshy Bridge expanded and its Load Meshy Bridge button highlighted](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/zplugin-menu.webp)

After a few seconds, a **Meshy** menu appears in the ZBrush menu bar. It holds all the bridge controls.

## Next steps
- To send your first model from Meshy to ZBrush, see [Bridge to ZBrush](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/bridge-to-zbrush).
